## balance-sheet-survival / 02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing.md`_

# Maturity Wall & Refinancing — BURL

Burlington Stores, Inc. is a U.S. GAAP operating company. Amounts below are USD millions at 1 August 2026 unless stated otherwise. This report uses the module's financial-debt basis: Term Loan Facility + convertible notes + finance leases, excluding $3,992.6m of operating-lease liabilities. That is $1,919.5m gross debt, matching `01_capital-structure-and-leverage`; it is not Capital IQ's $5,906.1m total-debt measure, which includes operating leases. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, filed 2026-08-27, pp.5, 10, 12–14; CIQ Financials→Balance Sheet `Total Debt` [Q2 2026-08-01] — vendor export]

## 1. Maturity Schedule

| Period | Amount Due | % of Total Debt | Instrument(s) | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Within 12 months (to 2027-08-01) | 20.1 | 1.0% | $17.5m Term Loan Facility amortisation + $2.6m current finance-lease liability | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, p.12; Note 3, p.10] |
| Year 2 (2027-08-02 to 2028-08-01) | 203.6 | 10.6% | $186.1m 1.25% convertible notes due 2027-12-15 + $17.5m Term Loan Facility amortisation | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13; FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 4—Scheduled Maturities] |
| Year 3 | 17.5 | 0.9% | Term Loan Facility amortisation | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 4—Scheduled Maturities; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Year 4 | 17.5 | 0.9% | Term Loan Facility amortisation | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 4—Scheduled Maturities; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Year 5 | 17.5 | 0.9% | Term Loan Facility amortisation | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 4—Scheduled Maturities; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Thereafter / finance-lease allocation not separately disclosed | 1,643.2 | 85.6% | $1,624.0m calculated residual Term Loan Facility due 2031-09-24 + $19.2m non-current finance-lease liability. The latter is a reconciliation item, not an assertion that all finance leases fall after Year 5. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, pp.10–11; Note 4, pp.12–13; FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 4—Scheduled Maturities] |
| **Total** | **1,919.5** | **100.0%** | **Financial debt including finance leases; excluding operating leases** | **[Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5, 10, 12–13]** |

The Term Loan Facility's $17.5m annual scheduled-amortisation amount comes from the latest audited schedule. The Q2 filing confirms the unchanged 2031 maturity and a $1,711.7m recorded Term Loan balance after two quarters of amortisation. The exact principal timing of the $19.2m non-current finance-lease liability is not separately disclosed, although its undiscounted payments are disclosed; it is therefore not invented into annual principal buckets. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 4—Scheduled Maturities; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, pp.10–11; Note 4, pp.12–13]

**CIQ-sidecar reconciliation.** The source-bound CIQ facts sidecar reports a vendor maturity read of “dated debt $2,067m of $6,013m total principal,” including $51m in 2026, $297m of 2027 converts and $1,719m in 2031. That is the authoritative read of the workbook's FY2026 as-reported detail, but it predates the 2026-02-09 repayment of the $50.6m promissory note and the March exchange of $111.0m of converts. The later Q2 filing reports $186.1m remaining converts and $1,711.7m Term Loan debt; the filing therefore governs this August-2026 schedule. CIQ's current $5,906.1m total debt also includes operating leases and is not interchangeable with the $1,919.5m financial-debt schedule. [CIQ Financials→Capital Structure Details, FY2026 as-reported block — vendor export; CIQ facts sidecar, `debt_maturity_wall` and `total_debt_m`, status present; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13]

## 2. Maturity Profile Metrics

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Weighted-average maturity (years) | **~4.7 years (estimated)** |
| % due within 12 months | **1.0%** |
| % due within 24 months | **≥11.7%** |
| % due within 36 months | **≥12.6%** |
| Largest single maturity year (and amount) | **2031: $1,624.0m Term Loan residual (84.6% of financial debt), due 2031-09-24** |

The 12-month share is exact: `$20.144m / $1,919.498m = 1.0%`. The 24- and 36-month figures are minimums: `($20.144m + $203.596m) / $1,919.498m = 11.7%` and `($20.144m + $203.596m + $17.525m) / $1,919.498m = 12.6%`; they exclude the unallocated portion of long-term finance leases rather than assign a date the filing does not give. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, pp.10–11; Note 4, pp.12–13]

The estimated weighted-average maturity (WAM) is reproducible but not a filed metric: `(17.525×0.5 + 17.525×1.5 + 17.525×2.5 + 17.525×3.5 + 17.525×4.5 + 1,624.033×5.15 + 186.071×1.37 + 2.618×0.5 + 19.151×11.3) / 1,919.498 = 4.72 years`. The $19.151m non-current finance lease is placed at its reported 11.3-year weighted-average remaining lease term as a proxy, not as a reported debt-payment WAM; changing that small component does not change the conclusion that the 2031 term-loan bullet dominates. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, pp.10–11; Note 4, pp.12–13]

## 3. Rate Exposure

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Fixed-rate share — contractual | 10.8% ($186.1m converts + $21.8m finance leases) | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, p.10; Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Floating-rate share — contractual | 89.2% ($1,711.7m Term Loan Facility) | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Economically fixed / hedged share | 68.1%: $1,100.0m Term Loan swaps + contractual fixed debt | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 5, p.14; Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Residual floating exposure after swaps | 31.9% ($611.7m) | `$1,711.7m − $1,100.0m`; [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 5, p.14; Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Weighted-average contractual cash coupon | 5.08% | `($1,711.658m×5.5% + $186.071m×1.25%) / $1,897.729m`; finance-lease discount rate excluded because it is not a debt coupon. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, p.10; Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Current market refi rate (five-year fixed-rate proxy) | 6.74% | 2026-09-25 five-year U.S. Treasury yield of 4.99% + BURL's current 1.75% secured Term Loan margin. This is an indicative proxy, not a BURL market quote. [Web: Mortgage News Daily, 5-Year U.S. Treasury Yield, 2026-09-25 (indicative, unverified); Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Estimated refi cost step-up | **+166 bps** | `6.74% − 5.08%`; indicative, not a committed refinancing quote. |

The $1.1bn swap book fixes rates at a weighted 3.23% through the 2031 Term Loan maturity. It reduces the estimated all-in, swap-adjusted financial-debt rate to 3.77%, but it does not make the underlying Term Loan fixed-rate debt. The residual $611.7m still reprices; a 100-basis-point move would change annual cash interest by roughly $6.1m (`$611.7m × 1%`), before any timing effects. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 5, p.14; Note 4, pp.12–13]

For a floating replacement, the latest web SOFR fixing of 3.90% plus the existing 1.75% Term Loan margin gives a separate 5.65% proxy, or +57 bps against the contractual 5.08% coupon. Against the 3.77% swap-adjusted cost, the five-year proxy is +297 bps. Neither calculation proves BURL can retain the current 1.75% credit margin or transfer its swaps into a new facility. [Web: SOFRRate.com, SOFR, 2026-09-25 (indicative, unverified); Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–13]

## 4. Refinancing Exposure

### Refi Funding Plan (no speculation)

| Source of repayment for next-24m maturities | Amount | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Cash on hand | 703.7 | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.5] |
| Recent FCF run-rate, not a forecast | 412.5 over latest TTM | CFO $1,415.5m less cash capex $1,002.9m; this is a historical run-rate, not funds committed to debt repayment. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5–6; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.45–46] |
| Revolver availability | 942.0 | Committed ABL availability at 2026-08-01, subject to the borrowing base; no draw was outstanding. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.13–14] |
| Asset-sale proceeds | Unknown — none announced in the data pool | Not proven from available data. |
| New debt issuance | Unknown — none committed or announced for the 2027 converts | Not proven from available data. |

The next 24 months contain at least $223.7m of debt maturities, while cash alone was $703.7m, or 3.15 times that amount; the historical TTM FCF and $942.0m of disclosed ABL availability are additional, not additive assumptions. The $186.1m convert due in December 2027 is the only material near-term cash maturity and is at the Parent, whose cash access depends on subsidiaries; the exact distribution baskets are not disclosed. The company extended the ABL to July 2030 in July 2025 and added $500m of Term B-7 loans in June 2025, which is evidence of recent market access but not a current refinancing commitment. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5–6, 30–32; Note 4, pp.12–14; FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1]

No current rating-agency rationale or action is in the admitted pool, so rating posture is not assessable from primary evidence. A web tenant-credit compilation dated April 2026 lists Burlington Coat Factory Warehouse Corp. as Ba1/BB+ with stable outlooks, but this is unverified and does not establish BURL's current market spread. **Conclusion: self-funded / low refi risk** for the next 12–24 months; the much larger 2031 bullet still depends on market access at that later date. [Web: Hanley Investment Group, Tenant Credit Ratings Q2 2026, 2026-04 (indicative, unverified)]

## 5. Refinancing Read

Only $20.1m is due in the next 12 months and at least $223.7m within 24 months, versus $703.7m cash; the refinancing issue is therefore timing and future cost, not a near-term wall. The $1.624bn calculated 2031 Term Loan residual is 84.6% of financial debt, and the five-year 6.74% proxy is 166 bps above the 5.08% contractual weighted coupon, or 297 bps above the 3.77% swap-adjusted rate. The single biggest risk is that the 2031 bullet must be refinanced at a wider credit spread or after the swap protection ends; its actual future market spread is not proven from available data.

BURL survives the next 12 months under a market-closure assumption of no new unsecured issuance: $20.1m of stated current debt is covered 34.9 times by consolidated cash before using the $942.0m disclosed ABL availability. This assumes that consolidated cash and the ABL remain legally available to the relevant borrowers and that optional buybacks are suspended; the filing does not quantify all Parent/subsidiary distribution constraints. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5, 30–32; Note 4, pp.12–14; FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1]

## balance-sheet-survival / 03_liquidity-runway.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/03_liquidity-runway.md`_

# Liquidity Runway — BURL

All amounts are USD millions. Burlington Stores, Inc. reports under U.S. GAAP. Balance-sheet liquidity is measured at 1 August 2026; cash-generation figures are latest-twelve-month (LTM) run rates to that date, not management forecasts.

## 1. Liquidity Sources (committed only)

| Source | Amount | Usable? | Notes | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Cash & equivalents | 703.7 | Y, subject to unquantified legal-entity restrictions | No separate restricted-cash balance is reported. The filing does not quantify whether any cash is trapped at a subsidiary, so full Parent-level usability is not separately proven. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, filed 2026-08-27, p.5; p.30] |
| Liquid short-term investments | 0.0 separately reported | N/A | The $703.7m total cash-and-short-term-investments read is entirely cash and equivalents; the separately reported $44.0m long-term investment balance is not labelled short-term or liquid and is excluded. | [Capital IQ Financials Annual workbook, Balance Sheet, Q2 2026-08-01 — vendor export; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.5] |
| Revolver / facilities (commitment) | 1,000.0 | Not counted separately | Committed ABL facility. Its headline commitment is not added to liquidity because current availability is disclosed below. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.13–14] |
| Revolver availability (if disclosed) | 942.0 | Y | No ABL borrowings were outstanding. Availability is subject to the borrowing base; no minimum-liquidity reserve or springing-covenant trigger is disclosed in the data pool. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.13–14] |
| **Total usable liquidity** | **1,645.7** |  | **$703.7m cash + $942.0m disclosed ABL availability. The facility is counted once, at availability rather than its $1.0bn commitment.** | **[Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.5; Note 4, pp.13–14]** |

No uncommitted line is disclosed in the admitted pool. The $942.0m ABL amount is committed capacity available at the snapshot, not cash already held; it can change with the inventory and receivables borrowing base.

## 2. Near-Term Uses (next 12 months)

| Use | Amount | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Debt maturities (from 02) | 20.1 | $17.5m Term Loan amortisation plus $2.6m current finance-lease liability, due by 1 August 2027. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, p.12; Note 3, p.10; balance-sheet-survival/02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing] |
| Cash interest | 73.1 FY2025 actual; LTM cash-paid figure not separately reconstructed | The latest annual cash-interest payment was $73.1m. Gross LTM interest expense was $74.1m, but that is not substituted for cash interest. This line is context only in the net-of-FCF calculation. [CIQ Financials Annual workbook, Cash Flow, FY2025 — vendor export; CIQ Financials→Income Statement, LTM 2026-08-01 — vendor export] |
| Maintenance capex | Not disclosed | BURL does not separate maintenance from growth capex. Its FY2026 total-capex plan is about $875m net of landlord allowances, including about $445m for stores and $290m for supply-chain initiatives; it cannot be relabelled maintenance capex. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Capital Expenditures, p.30; earnings/06_earnings-quality] |
| Committed dividends / buybacks | 0.0 | BURL paid no dividend and says it does not expect to pay one in the near term. The $217.6m remaining repurchase authorisation is discretionary, not a committed cash use, so it is excluded; $167.4m was repurchased in the first six months. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Dividends, p.30; Note 8, p.17] |
| **Total near-term uses** | **Not summed on a matched gross basis** | Maintenance capex is not disclosed and the available cash-interest figure is FY2025 rather than a forward 12-month commitment. The runway therefore uses the clean net-of-FCF basis below, which does not double-count either item. |

## 3. Runway

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Total committed liquidity | 1,645.7 |
| Annual FCF (or proxy) | 357.0 normalised operating FCF; 412.5 reported LTM FCF |
| Basis used (net-of-FCF / gross-obligations) | Net-of-FCF, using normalised FCF |
| Annual net cash burn (on the stated basis — see step 4) | **(336.9) — annual surplus, not burn** |
| Monthly net cash burn (annual burn ÷ 12) | **(28.1) — monthly surplus, not burn** |
| **Liquidity runway (months) = liquidity ÷ monthly net cash burn** | **No finite runway on this run-rate basis** |

FCF means CFO less total cash capex. Reported LTM FCF is `$1,415.5m CFO − $1,002.9m cash capex = $412.5m`. The source-bound CIQ facts sidecar confirms the $1,415.5m LTM CFO read; its $107.4m “levered FCF” is a different after-interest definition and is not used. The Q2 filing says CFO benefited by a $55.5m tariff refund, so the more conservative normalised operating FCF is `$412.5m − $55.5m = $357.0m`; this is an inference from the filing, not a reported company measure. [CIQ Financials→Cash Flow `Cash from Ops.`, LTM 2026-08-01 — vendor export; CIQ facts sidecar, `ltm_ocf_m`, status present; CIQ Financials→Cash Flow `Levered Free Cash Flow`, LTM 2026-08-01 — vendor export; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.45–46; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5–6, 20, 30]

Formula on the net-of-FCF basis: `annual net cash burn = (12-month maturities $20.1m + committed dividends/buybacks $0.0m) − normalised FCF $357.0m = $(336.9)m`. Cash interest and capex are already inside CFO/FCF, so adding the $73.1m historical cash-interest line or a capex proxy again would double-count. The resulting run-rate annual surplus is $336.9m, or $28.1m per month; it is not a forecast. Normalised FCF covers the stated 12-month debt maturities 17.7x, while cash alone covers them 34.9x. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, p.10; Note 4, p.12; earnings/01_historical-financials; earnings/06_earnings-quality]

### Seasonality / Peak Liquidity Need (Hard Check)

BURL is seasonal: Q4 generated an average 31.5% of annual revenue in FY2023–FY2025, and management says its retail business is seasonal. The filing reports working capital of $380.3m at 1 August 2026, but does not disclose a peak seasonal working-capital build or peak-quarter cash use that can be matched to a runway re-run. **Peak working-capital need not disclosed — runway may be overstated.** The $528.8m six-month cash use is not a peak-working-capital proxy because it also includes $537.7m of investing outflows and $325.7m of financing outflows. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1—Seasonality, p.5; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Liquidity and Capital Resources, p.30; earnings/01_historical-financials]

## 4. Sources & Uses Bridge

Internal sources cover the stated next-12-month debt use without a refinancing: reported consolidated cash of $703.7m is 34.9x the $20.1m maturity, and the normalised FCF run rate leaves a $336.9m annual surplus after that maturity. This read depends on $357.0m of FCF materialising; it is not all cash already in hand, and the filing does not quantify Parent-level cash restrictions. The additional $942.0m ABL availability is committed external draw capacity, not needed on this base case and subject to its borrowing base. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.5; Note 3, p.10; Note 4, pp.13–14; p.20; p.30]

## 5. Liquidity Read

There is no finite liquidity-runway end on the normalised LTM FCF basis: $1.646bn of committed liquidity and a $357.0m normalised FCF run rate sit against only $20.1m of stated financial-debt maturities over 12 months. The conclusion relies on operating cash continuing through a seasonal retailer’s peak inventory period; the $55.5m tariff refund is removed, but the peak working-capital build is not disclosed. The single biggest liquidity risk is a consumer, weather, or inventory shock that turns FCF negative while it also reduces ABL availability; $2.559bn of disclosed purchase commitments has no disclosed timing and could intensify that working-capital call, though it represents merchandise purchases rather than a disclosed loss. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.20; Item 2—Liquidity and Capital Resources, p.30; Note 11—Purchase Commitments, p.20; business-model/10_external-dependency]

## balance-sheet-survival / 04_coverage-and-covenants.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants.md`_

# Coverage & Covenants — BURL

Amounts are USD millions. Burlington is a U.S. GAAP operating retailer. Coverage uses Capital IQ standard LTM EBITDA of $1,360.7m rather than a BURL-reported GAAP EBITDA subtotal or company-adjusted EBITDA; the source-bound CIQ facts sidecar reports the same value. Gross interest expense is used, not net interest. [CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA` and `EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense`, LTM 12 months ended 2026-08-01 — vendor export]

## 1. Coverage Ratios

| Ratio | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| EBITDA / interest | 18.4x | `$1,360.7m ÷ $74.1m` gross interest. The sidecar's authoritative CIQ read is 18.4x. [CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense`, LTM 12 months ended 2026-08-01 — vendor export] |
| EBIT / interest | 12.8x | `$951.6m ÷ $74.1m`; EBIT is the CIQ operating-income calculation, not a BURL GAAP subtotal. [CIQ Financials Quarterly workbook, Income Statement, last four reported quarters through 2026-08-01 — vendor export] |
| (EBITDA − capex) / interest | 4.8x | `($1,360.7m − $1,002.9m) ÷ $74.1m`. Capex is total cash paid for property and equipment, not an estimate of maintenance capex. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.45–46; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.5–6; CIQ Financials Quarterly workbook, Income Statement — vendor export] |
| Fixed-charge coverage | 3.8x | Financial-debt proxy: `($1,360.7m − $1,002.9m) ÷ ($74.1m gross interest + $17.5m Term Loan amortization + $2.4m finance-lease principal)`. Operating-lease cash payments are already reflected in operating expense before EBITDA and are excluded to keep the ratio on a matched basis. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.45–46 and Note 3, p.65; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.5–6 and Note 3, p.10] |

Latest-TTM CFO of $1,415.5m exceeds the $1,360.7m CIQ standard EBITDA base, so the ratio is cash-backed at the CFO level. It is not a clean recurring-cash measure: reported TTM FCF of $412.5m includes a $55.5m tariff refund; the earnings-quality read estimates about $357.0m after removing that benefit. [CIQ Financials→Cash Flow `Cash from Ops.`, LTM 12 months ended 2026-08-01 — vendor export; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.20, 30; earnings/06_earnings-quality]

Calculation check (executed Bash/`awk`):

```text
EBITDA / gross interest = 18.36x
EBIT / gross interest = 12.84x
(EBITDA - capex) / gross interest = (1360.700 - 1002.936) / 74.100 = 4.83x
Financial-debt fixed-charge proxy = 357.764 / (74.100 + 17.526 + 2.381) = 3.81x
Indicative max-leverage headroom (4.0x / 4.5x) = 78.9% / 81.2%; EBITDA decline to threshold = 78.9% / 81.2%; debt increase = $4545.0m / $5265.1m
Illustrative min-coverage headroom (2.0x / 3.0x floors at 18.4x) = 820.0% / 513.3%
```

## 2. Covenant Inventory

The available filings do not disclose a live maintenance-covenant threshold, BURL's current covenant ratio, covenant EBITDA definition, addback caps, or equity-cure rights. The 3.50x consolidated-leverage condition disclosed in Schedule I gates restricted payments under the Term Loan Facility; it is not shown as a maintenance test, and the company does not disclose the current calculation. The ABL provides $942.0m of current availability and had no borrowing, but the filing does not state a springing-covenant trigger. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–14]

| Covenant | Threshold | Current Actual | Headroom | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Max net leverage | **Not disclosed.** Illustrative generic leveraged-borrower ceiling: 4.0–4.5x. | 0.84x using strict financial net debt of $1,215.8m / filing-derived LTM EBITDA of $1,440.2m; this is not a covenant calculation. | **Not assessable.** Illustrative 78.9%–81.2% under the stated generic ceiling. | *Inference, not from filings* for 4.0–4.5x; [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5, 10, 12–13; FY2025 Form 10-K, p.29; balance-sheet-survival/01_capital-structure-and-leverage] |
| Min interest coverage | **Not disclosed.** Illustrative generic floor: 2.0–3.0x. | 18.4x CIQ-standard EBITDA / gross interest; not a covenant definition. | **Not assessable.** Illustrative 513.3%–820.0% above the stated generic floor. | *Inference, not from filings* for 2.0–3.0x; [CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense`, LTM 12 months ended 2026-08-01 — vendor export] |
| Min liquidity / net worth | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.13–14] |
| Springing covenant trigger (e.g., revolver utilization threshold) | Not disclosed | ABL availability $942.0m; no ABL borrowings | Not assessable; active/not active cannot be determined | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.13–14] |
| Equity cure rights (Y/N, limits) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not assessable | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–14] |
| Other — restricted-payment condition | Consolidated leverage must not exceed 3.50x and no default for certain Term Loan distributions; ABL restricted-payment conditions also apply. | Not disclosed; the 0.84x accounting ratio above is not the contractual ratio. | Not assessable | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1] |

The generic thresholds above satisfy the partial-data rule only. They are not evidence that BURL has those covenants, so true covenant headroom remains **Not assessable** for scoring.

### Covenant EBITDA Definition & Quality (required if headroom is computed)

| Item | Value / Description | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Covenant EBITDA definition summary | Not disclosed in the data pool. The $1,360.7m coverage denominator is CIQ standard EBITDA, and the $1,440.2m illustrative leverage denominator is a filing-derived GAAP calculation; neither can be assumed to equal covenant EBITDA. | [CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA`, LTM 12 months ended 2026-08-01 — vendor export; FY2025 Form 10-K, p.29; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3, 20] |
| Addbacks permitted (types) | Not disclosed | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–14] |
| Addback caps / limits | Not disclosed | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–14] |
| Is covenant EBITDA materially above reported EBITDA? | Unknown. Headroom quality is unknown; there is an addback-illusion risk. | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–14] |

## 3. Headroom & Breach Proximity

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Tightest covenant | Not assessable — no maintenance covenant with a current contractual calculation is disclosed. |
| Headroom on tightest covenant (%) | Not assessable. |
| EBITDA decline that would breach it (approx.) | Not assessable. Illustrative only: 78.9%–81.2% if a 4.0–4.5x generic maximum-leverage test used strict net debt and filing-derived GAAP EBITDA, with debt and cash held constant. |
| Debt increase that would breach it (approx.) | Not assessable. Illustrative only: $4,545.0m–$5,265.1m of additional strict net debt on the same assumptions. |

The disclosed 3.50x ratio would restrict certain distributions if its contractual test fails, but the definition and present measurement are absent; it cannot be used to identify a breach point. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1]

## 4. Coverage / Covenant Read

Earnings cover gross interest 18.4x, while cash remaining after all reported capex covers it 4.8x; the financial-debt fixed-charge proxy is 3.8x. [CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense`, LTM 12 months ended 2026-08-01 — vendor export; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.45–46; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5–6]

The tightest covenant and contractual breach point are not assessable because BURL does not disclose maintenance thresholds, current covenant EBITDA, or addback limits. The only disclosed 3.50x condition is a restricted-payment condition, not evidence of live maintenance-covenant headroom; the next needed document is the current Term Loan/ABL credit agreement or compliance certificate. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 4, pp.12–14]

# Off-Balance-Sheet & Contingencies — BURL

All amounts are USD millions under U.S. GAAP, measured at August 1, 2026 unless stated otherwise. The $1,919.5m financial-debt stack in `01` includes finance leases but excludes operating leases; this report preserves that split.

## 1. Off-Balance-Sheet / Debt-Like Obligations

| Item | Recognized Liability | Maximum / Gross Exposure | Already in 01's debt? | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Operating leases, including committed but uncommenced sites | 3,992.6 | 5,735.1 = 5,124.6 future minimum payments + 610.5 for 99 stores and a New York buying-office floor not yet possessed | No — excluded from `01`'s strict financial-debt basis | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3 — Lease Commitments, pp.10–11] |
| Finance leases | 21.8 | 30.0 future payments (29.961 reported) | Yes — included in `01`'s $1,919.5m gross financial debt; excluded from the summary total below to avoid double-counting | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3 — Lease Commitments, pp.10–11; `01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md`, §1] |
| Pension / OPEB underfunding | Not disclosed; no defined-benefit or OPEB funded-status table identified | Not assessable | No | BURL describes defined-contribution 401(k) plans and $17.9m of FY2025 match expense, which is an operating expense rather than a plan deficit. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 11 — Employee Retirement Plans, p.66] |
| Securitization / receivables factoring | Not proven from available data | Not proven from available data | No | The Q2 filing says that, other than disclosed lease, purchase and debt items, there were no other significant changes in contractual payment obligations; it does not disclose a factoring or securitization amount. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2 — Certain Information Concerning Contractual Obligations, p.32] |
| Purchase commitments for goods not received | Not separately disclosed | 2,558.5 | No | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Purchase Commitments, p.20] |

The operating-lease gross figure is a rebuildable total: $5,124.643m of minimum payments plus $610.5m for signed but uncommenced leases. It is not a one-period cash call; the recognized lease liability is the discounted $3,992.562m amount, and the company also discloses sales-based contingent rent that is recognized only when incurred. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3 — Lease Commitments, pp.10–11]

The deterministic CIQ sidecar reports total debt of $5,906.1m. That vendor figure reconciles to the filing's $1,913.555m carrying amount of debt after deferred financing costs plus the $3,992.562m operating-lease liability (`$1,913.555m + $3,992.562m = $5,906.117m`, rounding to $5,906.1m). It is a lease-inclusive obligation measure, not a second liability or `01`'s strict debt measure. [CIQ Financials→Balance Sheet “Total Debt” [Q2 Aug-01-2026] — CIQ vendor basis; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3 — Lease Commitments, pp.10–11; Note 4 — Long-Term Debt, p.12]

## 2. Guarantees & Letters of Credit

| Item | Recorded | Maximum Exposure | Beneficiary / Purpose | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Standby letters of credit | Not separately disclosed | 58.0 outstanding: 57.9 for lease agreements, insurance contracts and utilities, plus 0.1 for merchandising agreements | Banks issue the letters; the named counterparties are not disclosed | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Letters of Credit, p.20] |
| Financial guarantees | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | No separate financial-guarantee amount is disclosed in the commitments note | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Commitments and Contingencies, p.20] |
| Performance / surety bonds | Not separately disclosed | Not separately disclosed | No separately disclosed surety-bond amount; the $57.9m performance letters above are the reported support for leases, insurance and utilities | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Letters of Credit, p.20] |

The $142.0m amount is the stated ability to enter additional letters of credit under the ABL agreement, not an outstanding draw exposure; it is not added to the $58.0m gross-exposure total. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Letters of Credit, p.20]

## 3. Litigation & Tax Contingencies

| Matter | Recorded Provision | Maximum / Claimed | Status (active / remote) | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Wage-and-hour, labor, California PAGA, commercial, product, employee, customer, IP, privacy and other proceedings | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Active: matters are in various procedural stages. BURL does not label them probable, reasonably possible or remote; it says it believes final resolution will not have a material adverse effect. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Legal, p.20; Item 1 — Legal Proceedings, p.35] |
| Unrecognized tax benefits and related interest / penalties | 4.3 of cumulative interest and penalties in other liabilities at FY2025 year-end; balance-sheet placement of the 1.566 gross unrecognized-tax-benefit amount is not separately stated | 1.6 gross unrecognized tax benefits (1.566 reported), not a disclosed maximum claim | Not classified as active, probable, reasonably possible or remote. The latest quantified uncertain-tax-position disclosure is the FY2025 annual filing; the Q2 tax note does not update it. | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 12 — Income Taxes, pp.68–69; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 — Income Taxes, pp.16–17] |

## 4. Contingent Exposure Summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Total recognized contingent liabilities | 3,992.6 current-date known amount: operating-lease liability at August 1, 2026. Finance leases are excluded because `01` already includes them in debt. |
| Total maximum / gross exposure | 8,351.6 current-date known contractual exposure = 5,124.643 operating-lease minimum payments + 610.5 uncommenced leases + 2,558.5 purchase commitments + 58.0 outstanding letters of credit. Finance-lease payments of 29.961 are excluded because `01` already includes that debt. |
| Max exposure ÷ recognized | 2.09x = 8,351.643 ÷ 3,992.562 |
| Max exposure ÷ total equity | 417.1% = 8,351.643 ÷ 2,002.248 total stockholders’ equity |

The summary deliberately excludes the $1.566m gross uncertain-tax-position figure and $4.3m related interest / penalties because their latest disclosed date is January 31, 2026, not the August 1 balance-sheet date; they remain in Section 3. The gross-exposure numerator is a mix of discounted and undiscounted multi-year contractual payments, merchandise that would become inventory, and letters of credit. It is therefore an exposure-size measure, not an estimate of a simultaneous loss or cash payment. Total equity is $2,002.248m at August 1, 2026. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.5; Note 3, pp.10–11; Note 11, p.20; FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 12, pp.68–69]

## 5. Contingency Read

The largest debt-like exposure is $5.735bn of gross operating-lease commitments, of which $610.5m is for signed sites not yet occupied; $3.993bn is already recognized, but future minimum payments exceed that discounted liability. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3 — Lease Commitments, pp.10–11] The $2.559bn goods commitment is live and large relative to $2.002bn of equity, but it purchases inventory rather than representing a disclosed loss; cash impact depends on delivery, sales conversion and working-capital timing. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Purchase Commitments, p.20; p.5] Legal proceedings are active and unquantified: management's view that final resolution will not be materially adverse is not the same as a remote classification. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Legal, p.20]

## balance-sheet-survival / 06_downside-stress-test.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/06_downside-stress-test.md`_

# Downside Stress Test — BURL

## 1. Base Case (today)

Burlington Stores, Inc. is a U.S. GAAP operating retailer. Amounts are USD millions and balance-sheet inputs are as of 1 August 2026; flow inputs are LTM to that date. The stress base uses $1,360.7m of Capital IQ standard EBITDA, rather than company-defined adjusted EBITDA. It is cash-backed at the CFO level: LTM CFO was $1,415.5m, though normalised FCF is only $357.0m after removing the $55.5m tariff-refund cash benefit. [ciq_facts.json, CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA` and Cash Flow `Cash from Ops.` [LTM 2026-08-01] — vendor export; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, p.20 and MD&A—Liquidity and Capital Resources, p.30]

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Base EBITDA (cash-backed) | 1,360.7 | CIQ standard LTM EBITDA; not a BURL-reported GAAP subtotal. LTM CFO of $1,415.5m exceeds it. [ciq_facts.json, CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA` and Cash Flow `Cash from Ops.` [LTM 2026-08-01] — vendor export] |
| Net debt | 1,215.8 strict | `$1,919.5m` financial gross debt less `$703.7m` cash and equivalents. This canonical strict basis includes finance leases and excludes operating leases. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, pp.5, 10, 12–13; balance-sheet-survival/01_capital-structure-and-leverage, §§1, 4] |
| Net debt / EBITDA | 0.89x | `$1,215.8m ÷ $1,360.7m`; strict net debt divided by CIQ standard LTM EBITDA. |
| EBITDA / interest | 18.4x | `$1,360.7m ÷ $74.1m` gross LTM interest expense. [ciq_facts.json, CIQ Financials→Income Statement `EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense` [LTM 2026-08-01] — vendor export; balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants, §1] |
| Tightest covenant + threshold | Not assessable contractually | No maintenance threshold, current covenant calculation, covenant-EBITDA definition, addback cap, springing trigger or cure right is disclosed. A 4.0x maximum **strict net-leverage** test is used below solely as the conservative end of `04`'s labelled generic 4.0–4.5x illustration; it is not BURL's disclosed covenant. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, pp.12–14; balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants, §§2–3] |
| Next-12m obligations | 20.1 | `$17.5m` Term Loan amortisation plus `$2.6m` current finance-lease liability. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, p.12; Note 3, p.10; balance-sheet-survival/02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing, §1] |
| Committed liquidity | 1,645.7 | `$703.7m` cash + `$942.0m` disclosed ABL availability. The ABL is subject to its borrowing base and is not cash in hand. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, p.5; Note 4, pp.13–14] |
| Floating-rate debt (gross) | 1,711.7 | Term Loan Facility is floating-rate at 5.5% at 1 August 2026. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, pp.12–13] |
| Hedge coverage | 1,100.0 notional | Interest-rate swaps hedge this Term Loan variable-rate exposure through 24 September 2031; residual floating exposure is `$611.7m`. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 5, p.14; balance-sheet-survival/02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing, §3] |
| Working-capital seasonality / peak build | Peak build not disclosed | Working capital was `$380.3m` at 1 August, while Q4 produced 31.5% of FY2023–FY2025 annual revenue on average. The filing does not disclose a matched peak build; the working-capital shock below is therefore an assumption. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, MD&A—Liquidity and Capital Resources, p.30; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-K(Mar-19-2026).doc, FY2025, Item 1—Seasonality, p.5] |

The $5,202.4m CIQ net-debt figure is not used in the stress base: it includes the $3,992.6m U.S.-GAAP operating-lease liability. That is a valid lease-inclusive vendor obligation measure, but not strict or broad §15 net debt. Operating leases remain a material fixed-cost risk; normal operating-lease cash payments are already within CFO/FCF and are not added again to the 12-month cash-use line. [ciq_facts.json, CIQ Financials→Balance Sheet `Net Debt` [Q2 2026-08-01] — vendor export; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, pp.5, 10–11]

No pending material business acquisition was identified in the admitted filing set or in `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance`; no pro-forma debt or EBITDA adjustment is therefore applied. This is limited to the frozen evidence pool. BURL's current investment programme is presented as stores, supply chain and IT capex. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-K(Mar-19-2026).doc, FY2025, Item 7—Capital Expenditures, p.33; business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance, §1]

FCF scaling for the stress is an inference, not from filings: `stressed FCF(h) = $357.038m − ($1,360.7m × h × 74.8%)`, where `h` is the EBITDA decline and 74.8% is one minus BURL's FY2025 25.2% effective tax rate. It holds cash interest and total capex fixed and lets only the after-tax EBITDA loss flow through to FCF. This is deliberately harsh because it assumes no price action, cost cut, capex cut, or sourcing offset. The remaining $217.6m repurchase authorisation is discretionary rather than a committed 12-month use, so it is not modeled as either an outflow or a mitigating cut. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-K(Mar-19-2026).doc, FY2025, MD&A—Income Taxes; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, p.20 and p.30; earnings/06_earnings-quality, §§1–2; balance-sheet-survival/03_liquidity-runway, §2]

## 2. Stress Scenarios

`12-month liquidity gap = uses ($20.1m maturity) − [reported usable liquidity + stressed FCF]`; a negative result is a surplus. The contractual covenant result remains **Not assessable** throughout. To make the balance-sheet sensitivity visible, the table also shows a clearly labelled, non-contractual 4.0x maximum-strict-net-leverage illustration. BURL is consumer-, weather- and inventory-exposed rather than classified as a deep commodity cycle; the −60% case is the severe survival bound. [business-model/10_external-dependency, §§1, 3; earnings/03_margin-drivers, §§1–2]

| Metric | Base | −30% EBITDA | −40% EBITDA | −60% EBITDA | −40% + WC shock | −40% + rates +200bp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| EBITDA | 1,360.7 | 952.5 | 816.4 | 544.3 | 816.4 | 816.4 |
| Net debt / EBITDA | 0.89x | 1.28x | 1.49x | 2.23x | 2.24x | 1.50x |
| EBITDA / interest | 18.36x | 12.85x | 11.02x | 7.35x | 11.02x | 9.46x |
| Tightest covenant headroom | Not assessable; illustrative 4.0x: 77.7% | Not assessable; illustrative: 68.1% | Not assessable; illustrative: 62.8% | Not assessable; illustrative: 44.2% | Not assessable; illustrative: 44.1% | Not assessable; illustrative: 62.4% |
| Covenant breach? (Y/N) | Not assessable; illustrative N | Not assessable; illustrative N | Not assessable; illustrative N | Not assessable; illustrative N | Not assessable; illustrative N | Not assessable; illustrative N |
| 12-month liquidity gap | $(1,982.6)m surplus | $(1,677.2)m surplus | $(1,575.5)m surplus | $(1,371.9)m surplus | $(965.5)m surplus | $(1,563.2)m surplus |
| Survives without equity raise, distressed asset sale, or covenant waiver? | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y |

Working-capital shock: the filing does not disclose peak seasonal cash usage, so this is a labelled 5% of LTM revenue assumption: `5% × $12,198.6m = $609.9m`. It is treated as an immediate cash use, which raises strict net debt by $609.9m and reduces usable liquidity by the same amount. The ABL is held at its reported $942.0m availability because no borrowing-base sensitivity is disclosed; a real inventory or receivable shock could change it. [Capital IQ Financials Quarterly workbook, Income Statement, LTM 2026-08-01 — vendor export; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, pp.13–14]

Rate shock: after the $1.1bn swaps, `$611.7m × 2% = $12.2m` of extra annual cash interest. This scenario deducts the full $12.2m from FCF and adds it to strict net debt, with no tax shield, and uses `$86.3m` interest for coverage. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, pp.12–13; Note 5, p.14]

All scenarios assume zero management mitigation — this is a survival bound, not a forecast; `earnings/07` §2 supplies the expected-outcome sensitivity framework, but it does not disclose a measured realised offset for BURL's demand or merchandise shocks.

The executed calculation was:

```text
$ awk 'BEGIN {e=1360.7; nd=1215.812; intr=74.1; liq=1645.686; mat=20.144; fcf=357.038; keep=.748; wc=.05*12198.6; rate=(1711.658-1100)*.02; for(i=0;i<4;i++){h=(i==0?0:(i==1?.3:(i==2?.4:.6))); eb=e*(1-h); sf=fcf-e*h*keep; print sprintf("%3.0f%%: EBITDA %.1f | leverage %.2fx | coverage %.2fx | 4.0x headroom %.1f%% | gap %.1f",100*h,eb,nd/eb,eb/intr,100*(4-nd/eb)/4,mat-liq-sf)} h=.4; eb=e*(1-h); sf=fcf-e*h*keep; print sprintf("40%%+WC: EBITDA %.1f | leverage %.2fx | coverage %.2fx | 4.0x headroom %.1f%% | gap %.1f",eb,(nd+wc)/eb,eb/intr,100*(4-(nd+wc)/eb)/4,mat-(liq-wc)-sf); print sprintf("40%%+rates: EBITDA %.1f | leverage %.2fx | coverage %.2fx | 4.0x headroom %.1f%% | gap %.1f",eb,(nd+rate)/eb,eb/(intr+rate),100*(4-(nd+rate)/eb)/4,mat-liq-(sf-rate)); print sprintf("breaks: illustrative 4.0x %.1f%% | liquidity %.1f%% | 6.0x %.1f%%",100*(1-nd/(4*e)),100*((liq+fcf-mat)/(e*keep)),100*(1-nd/(6*e)))}'
  0%: EBITDA 1360.7 | leverage 0.89x | coverage 18.36x | 4.0x headroom 77.7% | gap -1982.6
 30%: EBITDA 952.5 | leverage 1.28x | coverage 12.85x | 4.0x headroom 68.1% | gap -1677.2
 40%: EBITDA 816.4 | leverage 1.49x | coverage 11.02x | 4.0x headroom 62.8% | gap -1575.5
 60%: EBITDA 544.3 | leverage 2.23x | coverage 7.35x | 4.0x headroom 44.2% | gap -1371.9
40%+WC: EBITDA 816.4 | leverage 2.24x | coverage 11.02x | 4.0x headroom 44.1% | gap -965.5
40%+rates: EBITDA 816.4 | leverage 1.50x | coverage 9.46x | 4.0x headroom 62.4% | gap -1563.2
breaks: illustrative 4.0x 77.7% | liquidity 194.8% | 6.0x 85.1%
```

## 3. Break Points

| Break Point | EBITDA Decline That Triggers It |
|---|---:|
| Tightest covenant breaches | **Not assessable.** No contractual maintenance threshold or covenant EBITDA is disclosed. Under the labelled 4.0x maximum-strict-net-leverage illustration, 77.7%. |
| Committed liquidity exhausted within 12 months | **Does not exhaust on an EBITDA decline alone.** The mechanical solve is 194.8%, beyond a possible 100% EBITDA fall. |
| Net leverage exceeds 6.0x | 85.1% under a labelled 6.0x refinancing-risk marker; this is neither a BURL covenant nor a disclosed lender threshold. |

The illustrative covenant is a MAX/ceiling test using the stated generic numerator, strict net debt: `h = 1 − ND ÷ (T × EBITDA) = 1 − 1,215.812 ÷ (4.0 × 1,360.7) = 77.7%`. It must not be read as a contractual BURL breach point. The filing's disclosed 3.50x condition limits certain distributions, but neither its calculation nor whether it is a maintenance test is disclosed. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-K(Mar-19-2026).doc, FY2025, Schedule I, Note 1; balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants, §§2–3]

Liquidity uses `1,645.686 + [357.038 − (1,360.7 × h × 0.748)] = 20.144`, so `h = (1,645.686 + 357.038 − 20.144) ÷ (1,360.7 × 0.748) = 194.8%`. At a full 100% EBITDA loss, the same zero-mitigation scaling still leaves about `$964.8m` after the $20.1m stated maturity; that is a model result, not a forecast. The 6.0x marker is the same MAX form: `h = 1 − 1,215.812 ÷ (6.0 × 1,360.7) = 85.1%`. The executed `awk` output in Section 2 is the calculation record for these solves.

## 4. Survival Read

On the stated strict financial-debt basis, no modeled cash break occurs through a 60% EBITDA decline: at −60%, net leverage is 2.23x, EBITDA covers gross interest 7.35x, and the 12-month cash result is a `$1.372bn` surplus. The first modeled threshold is the non-contractual 4.0x illustration at a 77.7% EBITDA decline; the real covenant breach point is **Not assessable** until BURL's current Term Loan/ABL agreement or compliance certificate is available. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, pp.12–14; balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants, §§2–4]

The 30–40% recession-style haircuts survive on their own under this zero-mitigation bound, including a $609.9m assumed working-capital call at −40%; that combined case retains a `$965.5m` 12-month surplus. The important qualification is that the reported $942.0m ABL availability is borrowing-base-dependent and that $2.559bn of purchase commitments have no disclosed timing. Those commitments are merchandise purchases rather than a stated loss and cannot be added mechanically to FCF without double counting, but an extreme inventory or vendor-payment shock could make the reported ABL availability less usable. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, Note 4, pp.13–14; Note 11, p.20]

Market closure test: assuming no new unsecured refinancing for 12 months, the $20.1m scheduled financial-debt maturity is covered by reported cash and disclosed ABL capacity; no equity raise, distressed asset sale or covenant waiver is modeled as necessary. This does not settle the Parent-versus-subsidiary cash-access constraint or the later $1.624bn 2031 Term Loan bullet, and it excludes any unreported deterioration in the ABL borrowing base. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, Q2 FY2026, p.30; Note 4, pp.12–14; balance-sheet-survival/02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing, §§1, 5]

# Competitive-Intel Module — BURL (Synthesis)

## Abstract

The frozen pool holds only the named peer set—Ross and TJX—and no usable competitor call or permitted broker paraphrase, so it does not provide a real peer benchmark. The net read-through for BURL’s Q3 FY2026 print is Not assessable; with no eligible peer, its weight and direction confidence are also Not assessable. BURL’s own demand, pricing, margin, input-cost and guidance narrative is not testable against peers, so neither corroboration nor contradiction can be claimed. Eligible peers cover 0% of BURL’s sole U.S. off-price segment, leaving the entire business outside the benchmark. Verdict: insufficient benchmark evidence; this module should not move the master beat/miss or candor view.

## 1. Verdict Block

- **Net read-through direction:** Not assessable. A sourced BURL revenue bar exists, but there is no eligible peer signal with which to test it.
- **Operational direction:** Not assessable; no admitted competitor call supports an operations-up, operations-down or mixed inference.
- **Read-through weight:** Not assessable. With zero eligible peers, no High / Medium / Low weight exists to carry.
- **Read-through direction confidence:** Not assessable. There is no direction to assign a §10 probability band or basis.
- **Narrative triangulation verdict:** Not testable.
- **Peer-coverage of subject /100:** 0.
- **Benchmark data-sufficiency /100:** 0.
- **Dispersion:** Not assessable.
- **Single most important peer signal:** None; the frozen pool contains no admitted Ross or TJX call, results release or permitted broker call paraphrase.
- **Biggest contradiction or corroboration of the subject’s narrative:** None testable; missing peer evidence is neither corroboration nor contradiction.

The frozen manifest contains 30 source rows, zero external rows and no failed extractions. The two calls in the pool are BURL’s own calls, not peer evidence. Ross and TJX are the competitive map’s named public U.S. off-price peers. [Frozen pool manifest (data/BURL/, generation `fc90a997f0c1c57b475af85d46d5fac22d04f645a3d926655acba4ef4b26f766`), Sources; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — BURL, §§1, 3]

## 1B. Score Builds (reproducible — CLAUDE.md §12)

**Peer-coverage of subject /100 = 0.** Covered exposure is 0%: no segment or geography has a read-through-eligible, scope-overlapping peer on a matched window. `round(0%) = 0`. The uncovered exposure is BURL’s sole U.S. off-price retail segment, which represents 100.0% of FY2025 revenue. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 1 — Segment Information; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — BURL, §2]

| Benchmark data-sufficiency component | Build | Points |
|---|---|---:|
| Reporting-peer breadth | N = 0 distinct eligible peers; N = 0 maps to 0 | 0 / 40 |
| Exposure coverage | `round(0% × 0.30) = 0` | 0 / 30 |
| Source quality | No eligible verbatim transcript and no eligible broker paraphrase | 0 / 20 |
| Peer-set provenance | Ross and TJX come from `business-model/08_competitive-map.md`, not a self-selected set | 10 / 10 |
| **Component subtotal** | `0 + 0 + 0 + 10` | **10 / 100** |
| **No-usable-call floor** | No verbatim peer transcript and no permitted broker paraphrase; this non-additive rule overrides the subtotal | **0 / 100** |
| **Final benchmark data-sufficiency** | No-usable-call floor applied | **0 / 100** |

Neither score is inverted; higher means broader coverage or better benchmark sufficiency. The provenance points preserve the fact that the peer set was independently established, but the no-usable-call floor prevents peer names without evidence from becoming a benchmark. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — BURL, §§1, 3–5; Competitive Map — BURL, §2]

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation (CLAUDE.md §8)

- **Strongest bear read-through:** Not assessable; no peer management signal or peer reported figure is admitted.
- **Strongest bull read-through:** Not assessable for the same reason.
- **Single killer contradiction:** None testable. An absent peer source cannot contradict BURL.
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** None in peer calls; there are no eligible peer calls.
- **What data would change this conclusion:** No peer-derived BURL line-item boundary exists to carry forward. The $2,992.38m CIQ FQ3 2027 / company Q3 FY2026 revenue consensus is a subject estimate, not a confirmation or falsification test for an absent peer hypothesis. A future run would first need an admitted Ross or TJX management call covering an overlapping calendar window; only then could it define a BURL line item, boundary, year-earlier comparable and standalone-quarter basis. [data/BURL/BurlingtonStores,IncNYSEBURLEstimatesReport.xls, Consensus sheet, CIQ FQ3 2027; Peer Read-Through — BURL, §§4–5]
- **What would force a downgrade / rejection:** No further downgrade is possible because this module currently contributes no direction or weight. Any later peer read-through must be rejected if its source is outside the frozen corpus, its calendar window does not overlap BURL’s standalone 13 weeks ending October 31, 2026, or its scope does not overlap BURL’s U.S. off-price business.

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| competitive-intel-triage | **Insufficient.** | The pool has no usable competitor call or permitted broker paraphrase; eligible peers cover 0% of BURL’s 100%-of-revenue U.S. off-price segment. |
| peer-claim-extraction | **Insufficient — no usable competitor call in the pool.** | Ross and TJX each have 11 dimensions marked Not addressed; absence of a source was not turned into a management signal. |
| peer-dimension-matrix | **Insufficient — empty matrix.** | Zero eligible peers means no aligned-window cell, peer consensus, dispersion measure or named outlier. |
| peer-readthrough-to-subject | **Insufficient data — no usable competitor call in the pool.** | The $2,992.38m subject revenue bar exists, but no eligible peer evidence indicates whether BURL will clear it; direction, weight and confidence are Not assessable. |
| peer-narrative-triangulation | **Not testable.** | No peer claim can corroborate or contradict BURL’s demand, pricing, margin, input-cost, share or guidance narrative. |

## 3. Reconciliation

No material disagreements. All five specialists converge on an empty peer benchmark, 0% covered exposure, Not assessable read-through and Not testable narrative triangulation. The matrix’s Not assessable dispersion therefore does not conflict with the read-through verdict; both result from zero eligible peers, not from mixed peer evidence.

**Five-guardrail and claim-fidelity pass:** G1 — no peer period was compared, and the absence of an admitted call was kept as a corpus gap rather than recast as “not yet reported.” G2 — no peer-to-BURL inference was made. G3 — the 0% covered share and 100% uncovered U.S. off-price exposure remain explicit. G4 — no cross-peer absolute or ratio comparison was made. G5 — no analyst assertion or broker verdict entered the report. Claim qualifiers, bases and builds remain attached: no call means no signal, not proof of peer agreement, disagreement or public reporting status.

The Capital IQ relationship graph does not change this result. It is a tier-5 view of recently disclosed supplier relationships and current subsidiaries, not a source of competitive-peer management commentary; group entities are not treated as arm’s-length peers. [Capital IQ Suppliers/Customers relationship graph (data/BURL/, generation `fc90a997f0c1c57b475af85d46d5fac22d04f645a3d926655acba4ef4b26f766`), scope notes — vendor export; Peer Dimension Matrix — BURL, §3]

## 4. Score Cap Application

| Cap Trigger | Applied? (Y/N) | Affected | Final Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| No peer transcripts | Y | read-through | Not assessable |
| Only one peer | N | weight | No single-peer cap; there are zero peers and the stricter no-peer lock applies |
| No peer reported the window | Y — no comparable-window peer call is admitted; this is not a claim about public reporting status | current read-through | Not assessable |
| Exposure uncovered (by coverage band) | Y — covered exposure is 0%, below 30% | net weight | Low ceiling, superseded by the no-peer **Not assessable** lock |
| Peer set self-selected | N | net weight | No cap; peer set comes from the competitive map |
| Broker-paraphrase only | N | tone | No broker paraphrase exists; the stricter no-usable-call lock applies |

The deterministic exposure ceiling is Low because `covered_exposure_pct = 0%`, but a ceiling does not create a weight. With no eligible peer and no net direction, final weight and direction confidence both remain Not assessable.

## 5. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Carry **Net read-through: Not assessable; weight: Not assessable; direction confidence: Not assessable**. There is no peer signal to move BURL’s beat/miss or scenario view. The sourced $2,992.38m revenue bar does not change that because no peer hypothesis exists to test against it. [Peer Read-Through — BURL, §§4–5]
- Carry no peer-derived confirmation or falsification boundary into §8. No BURL line item, threshold, year-earlier comparable or reporting basis was built from peer evidence. The highest-value missing input is an admitted Ross or TJX management call that overlaps BURL’s standalone 13 weeks ending October 31, 2026.
- Treat BURL’s narrative as **Not testable**, not corroborated and not contradicted. Missing peer evidence supplies no governance or candor signal.
- Keep the coverage gap visible: peers speak to **0%**, and therefore cannot speak to **100%**, of BURL’s sole U.S. off-price segment in this run.
- The no-usable-call cap binds the result to Not assessable. The 0%-coverage rule would impose a Low ceiling if an eligible signal existed, but it cannot manufacture a weight from no evidence.

## 6. Simple Summary

- No. There are named peers, but no real peer call or permitted call summary to benchmark.
- The already-reported-peer implication for BURL’s next print is Not assessable; weight and probability are also Not assessable.
- BURL’s story does not pass or fail the peer check because the check cannot be run.
- The benchmark is blind to 100% of BURL’s U.S. off-price business.
- The module is useful only as a guardrail: it prevents the master from treating missing peer evidence as a beat/miss or candor signal.
- The next useful input is a Ross or TJX management call admitted into BURL’s frozen corpus and matched to the same calendar window and scope.

## management-governance — module synthesis

_Source: `management-governance/99_management-governance-synthesis.md`_

# Management-Governance Module — BURL (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Burlington’s management looks competent, but shareholder alignment is ordinary rather than owner-like. The team met or exceeded all three completed targets reviewed, while four-year capital spending and buybacks supported operating growth and reduced diluted shares, though strict net debt rose and repurchases were not tested against intrinsic value. Pay is tied mainly to adjusted EBIT and adjusted EPS, yet insiders own only 1.3%, logged no open-market buys, and were net sellers. The clearest governance concern is repeated adjusted-profit exclusions, including $21.8 million in FY2025, alongside a coverage-limited legal and people sweep. The resulting call is Standard / mixed: usable evidence, no gate failure, but not enough alignment or clean disclosure to call stewardship exemplary.

## 1. Stewardship Verdict

- **Verdict:** Standard / mixed
- **NON-NEGOTIABLE GATE: PASS** — no hard disqualifier, Critical module red flag, Disqualifying-graded controller/CEO/CFO/chair, or material undisclosed legal matter was evidenced. Coverage is 131/179 registry items answered.
- **Hard disqualifier flagged (business-model/01)?** N — business-model/01 reports “No disqualifier triggered.”
- Management quality /100: 83
- Capital allocation /100: 68
- Incentive alignment /100: 79
- Shareholder friendliness /100: 71
- Disclosure candor /100: 68
- People & network integrity /100: 65 (79 before the mandatory coverage cap)
- Audit & assurance quality /100: 72
- RPT & leakage risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: 35
- Contingent-liability risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: 20
- Accounting-forensics risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: 25
- Legal & regulatory risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: 40
- Governance risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: 40
- Data quality /100: 78
- Overall usefulness /100: 82
- **Checklist coverage:** 131/179 (73.2%) — 48 Green / 80 Amber / 3 Red / 48 N-A
- Insider ownership (one line): directors and executives beneficially own 1.3%; the CEO owns about 0.74%, 72.1% of his disclosed position is options or near-term RSUs, and the reviewed year had five open-market sales, no open-market buys, and net sales of 9,231 shares. [FY2026 DEF 14A, Security Ownership; Form 4 review through 2026-09-29]
- Biggest governance signal (one line): all three completed operating targets reviewed were met or exceeded, but the people directing capital have thin purchased equity and no observed open-market buying. [01_management-and-track-record, Sections 2–3; 04_ownership-and-insider-behavior, Sections 1–3]
- **Checklist Risk:** max(35 RPT, 20 contingent-liability, 25 accounting-forensics, 40 legal/regulatory) = **40**, bound by Legal & regulatory risk.
- **Governance Score /100:** 0.14×68 + 0.11×79 + 0.11×71 + 0.10×68 + 0.11×83 + 0.09×72 + 0.11×65 + 0.11×(100−40) + 0.12×(100−40) = 69.38, reported as **69**.
- **Confidence-Adjusted Governance Score /100:** 69 × 70 / 100 = **48** (48.3 before whole-number reporting).
- **Governance Rating:** Watchlist
- **Confidence Score /100:** 70 — capped by the coverage-limited legal and person/entity database sweeps.
- **Red-Flag Count / Critical Red-Flag Count:** 2 / 0

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** the incentive system uses absolute adjusted EBIT for the annual bonus, recurring adjusted-profit exclusions continued, and insiders recorded no open-market purchases; the FY2025 non-GAAP reconciliation excluded $21.8 million. [FY2026 DEF 14A, Compensation Discussion & Analysis; FY2025 Form 10-K, MD&A / non-GAAP reconciliation]
- **Strongest bull point:** management met or exceeded all three completed targets that the track-record specialist could test, while FY2025 CFO/PAT was 2.02× and CFO/EBITDA was 99.2%, so delivery is supported by cash rather than only adjusted profit. [01_management-and-track-record, Sections 2–3; earnings/06_earnings-quality, Sections 1–3]
- **Single killer risk:** debt-funded expansion and buybacks could be rewarded through adjusted EBIT and EPS even if per-share value weakens; this becomes thesis-killing stewardship evidence if leverage rises while repurchases fail to reduce diluted shares or cash returns deteriorate. [02_capital-allocation-scorecard, Sections 1–5; FY2026 DEF 14A, Compensation Discussion & Analysis]
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** a 91.7%-independent board, independent chair, clean current audit and ICFR opinions, $0 of FY2025 reportable Item 404 transactions, and no hard disqualifier argue against a negative integrity conclusion; historical auditor discipline and incomplete legal screens prevent calling the record clean. [FY2026 DEF 14A, Board and Certain Relationships; FY2025 Form 10-K, Auditor Report; business-model/01_disqualifier-scan]

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| governance-data-triage | Sufficient | Core proxy, ownership, board, RPT and multi-year capital-allocation inputs are present; formal annual-meeting voting results and complete legal/rating archives are missing. |
| management-and-track-record | 83/100 — capable, stable operating team | CEO tenure is seven years, CFO tenure 4.1 years, and all three completed targets tested were met or exceeded; the CHRO left with no disclosed successor. |
| capital-allocation-scorecard | 68/100 — mixed | FY2022–FY2025 capex was $2,880.2m, 80.9% of CFO; $1,094.8m of buybacks reduced diluted shares 2.69%, but strict net debt rose to $1,209.9m by Q2 FY2026. |
| incentives-and-compensation | 79/100 — mixed alignment | Annual bonus is 100% absolute adjusted EBIT; 65% of LTIP is adjusted-EPS PSUs, 35% is time-based RSUs, and potential overhang is 13.4%. |
| ownership-and-insider-behavior | 56/100 — thin purchased alignment | Insiders own 1.3%; no open-market buys and five sales produced net sales of 9,231 shares, while no controller or pledge was identified. |
| board-and-shareholder-rights | 71/100 — adequate | The board is 91.7% legally independent with an independent chair, but five directors exceed ten years and holders cannot call a special meeting or act by written consent. |
| candor-and-disclosure-quality | 68/100 — mixed | The $55m tariff refund and its $0.64 EPS effect were quantified, but recurring exclusions fired RF-DISC-002. |
| people-integrity-dossiers | 65/100 after cap — pass, coverage-limited | All 40 people were graded Clean on their own records, but identifier-linked registry, court, sanctions and PEP screens were incomplete. |
| audit-and-assurance-quality | 72/100 — sound current assurance with history to monitor | Current audit and ICFR opinions are clean and non-audit fees are 5.7% of audit fees; 43-year Deloitte tenure and three historical PCAOB orders fired RF-AUD-007. |
| related-party-and-group-forensics | 35/100 risk — low-to-moderate evidenced risk | FY2025 reportable Item 404 RPT was $0; the $297.1m BCFWC/BMC joint note is disclosed intragroup funding, not proven minority leakage. |
| contingent-liabilities-and-commitments | 20/100 risk — low quantified risk, incomplete categories | $58.0m of letters of credit equals 2.90% of Q2 equity; $2,558.5m of inventory commitments is separate from contingent loss and lacks cancellation detail. |

## 3. Reconciliation


- **Execution versus alignment:** management quality is 83 because the team delivered the three completed targets that could be tested, but capital allocation is 68, ownership alignment is 56, and insiders made no observed open-market buys. The conservative read is competent operators with conventional, not owner-like, alignment.
- **Board labels versus practical independence:** 91.7% of directors meet the legal independence test and the chair is independent, but five directors had tenure over ten years and shareholders cannot call a special meeting or act by written consent. The board is adequate, not exemplary.
- **Candor versus adjusted performance:** the tariff refund was quantified precisely, but repeated lease, impairment and litigation exclusions fired RF-DISC-002. The transparent single event does not erase the recurring adjusted-profit pattern.
- **Current audit quality versus gatekeeper history:** clean financial-statement and ICFR opinions and a 5.7% non-audit/audit fee ratio support the current assurance read; 43 years of tenure, historical PCAOB orders, and an unidentified signing partner keep A4-02 and A4-13 Red. No BURL-specific audit failure was established.
- **No reportable RPT versus group funding opacity:** the proxy reports $0 of FY2025 Item 404 transactions, while the 10-K shows a $297.1m joint note to BCFWC/BMC and 99.976% of consolidated cash below the Parent. These are disclosed intragroup facts with $409.0m of upstream contributions, not proof of minority leakage; entity-level cash and guarantee mapping remains missing.
- **Cash-supported earnings versus forensic gaps:** CFO/PAT of 2.02× and CFO/EBITDA of 99.2% support earnings, while DEPI, soft assets, flat cash taxes, and unmatched cash-interest data remain monitors. The measured battery is not Red.
- **Legal/person outcomes versus search coverage:** no person was attributed a Material or Disqualifying fact and the two public cases reconcile to filed legal categories, but the official regulator, court, sanctions, exchange, and rating interfaces were incomplete. “Nothing material found” is not a clearance.
- **Subsidiary count discrepancy:** 09 records 25 named subsidiaries, while 07’s scope-boundary prose refers to 26 current subsidiaries. No conclusion depends on the one-entity difference; obtain the legal-entity chart before using either count as a control threshold.

## 5. Stewardship Summary

Management has delivered the completed targets available for testing, and the cash record supports the operating result, but the evidence does not show an owner-operator culture. FY2022–FY2025 capital spending of $2,880.2 million absorbed 80.9% of CFO, while $1,094.8 million of buybacks reduced diluted shares 2.69%; strict net debt then rose from $849.8 million at FY2025 year-end to $1,209.9 million at Q2 FY2026, so future repurchases need a price-and-leverage test. Incentives point partly toward per-share value through adjusted-EPS PSUs, but an absolute adjusted-EBIT bonus, 35% time-based RSUs, 1.3% insider ownership, and no observed open-market buying weaken that link. Minority holders have one vote per share, an independent chair, and all-independent committees, but long director tenure and weak direct-action rights temper the protection. The best reason to trust this team is delivered execution backed by cash; the main reason not to grant higher confidence is that adjusted metrics, thin purchased ownership, and incomplete legal/person screens leave room for stewardship quality to look better than it is.

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer


- Stewardship is **Standard / mixed**: the strongest positive is three of three completed targets met or exceeded with cash-supported earnings; thin purchased ownership, adjusted-metric pay, and recurring exclusions prevent a higher call.
- **NON-NEGOTIABLE GATE: PASS** with 131/179 checklist items answered; none of the four gate conditions was evidenced.
- Capital allocation produced growth and a 2.69% diluted-share reduction, but $2,880.2m of four-year capex and $1,094.8m of buybacks must now be judged beside Q2 FY2026 strict net debt of $1,209.9m.
- Incentives partly target per-share value through adjusted-EPS PSUs, but annual bonus is absolute adjusted EBIT; insiders own 1.3%, made no observed open-market purchase, and were net sellers.
- **People read:** 40 Clean-on-own-record grades, all coverage-limited; no Minor, Material, or Disqualifying grades. The highest-priority unresolved issue is missing identifier-linked coverage, not an attributed adverse fact.
- **Checklist read:** 73.2% answered; Red items are A1-04, A4-02, and A4-13. Legal & regulatory risk at 40 is the binding Checklist Risk.
- Two unique High flags remain: RF-DISC-002 for recurring adjusted exclusions and RF-AUD-007 for historical audit-firm discipline. Critical count is zero.
- business-model/01 hard-disqualifier result, verbatim: **“No disqualifier triggered.”**
- No §24 turnaround, serial-acquirer, structurally unaligned-owner, or unresolved-integrity filter tripped; none imposed a conviction cap.
- The legal/person sweep coverage cap binds: People & network integrity 65, Legal risk 40, Confidence 70. Declared entity breadth overflow also caps People at 70 and Confidence at 80, but is not binding.
- Single highest-value next data request: an identifier-linked paid U.S. people-and-entity registry/court/sanctions/PEP/regulator batch for the 40-person roster, BURL’s former name, BCFWC, and BCF Direct.
- **This module supersedes business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance; use this synthesis verdict and scores as the primary governance read.**

## 8. Simple Summary


- Management met or beat every completed target the specialist could test.
- Capital spending and buybacks helped growth and reduced diluted shares, but debt rose; value creation is mixed, not proven.
- Pay rewards absolute adjusted EBIT and adjusted EPS, with 35% of long-term awards still time-based.
- Insiders own 1.3%, made no observed open-market buys, and were net sellers.
- Minority holders get one vote per share and an independent chair, but long board tenure and weak direct-action rights matter.
- Management quantified the tariff refund well, yet recurring adjusted exclusions weaken the candor read.
- No hard disqualifier or Critical red flag fired; the gate passes.
- The module is useful, but the master should cap confidence at 70 until legal and person/entity screens are complete.

## 6. Sufficiency Verdict

- **Verdict:** Sufficient
- **Reason:** The frozen pool has a current SEC proxy/compensation disclosure, beneficial-ownership and Form 4-sourced insider data, board and related-party disclosure, two annual filings plus multi-year financial history, an audit report and fee disclosure, and recent transcripts; all required core governance source types are present and extraction completed without failures.
- **Specialists that can run:** management track record; capital allocation; incentives; ownership; board; candor; people dossiers (with identifier and public-database work still required); audit quality; RPT/group forensics; contingent liabilities; accounting forensics; regulatory/legal (with public-database work still required).
- **Hard disqualifier already flagged by business-model/01_disqualifier-scan?** N — upstream scan says no disqualifier triggered.
- **Critical missing items:** formal AGM/annual-meeting voting-results filing; dedicated 8-K/exchange-compliance archive; primary rating-agency reports; and public legal/regulatory database sweep. These do not change the Sufficient verdict because the core proxy, ownership, board/RPT and multi-year capital-allocation requirements are met. The downstream owners must state coverage limits if their database sweep cannot run.
- **Single highest-value missing document:** formal 2026 annual-meeting voting-results filing (or the corresponding 8-K), because it is the missing direct evidence for minority dissent and resolution-level voting.

# Management & Track Record — BURL

## 1. Key Executives

| Role | Name | Appointed | Tenure | Relevant Background | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| CEO | Michael O’Sullivan | September 2019 | 7.0 years | Professional manager, not a founder: Burlington CEO since 2019; formerly Ross Stores’ President and COO (2009–2019), after retail-strategy work at Bain & Company (1991–2003). | [S01: FY2026 Proxy Statement, p. 19] |
| CFO | Kristin Wolfe | August 2022 | 4.1 years | Former Ross Stores Group SVP, Corporate Finance; prior finance, strategy and store-operations roles at Ross from 2009. | [S01: FY2026 Proxy Statement, p. 20] |
| Group President & Chief Merchandising Officer | Jennifer Vecchio | July 2021 in current role; joined Burlington May 2015 | 5.2 years in current role; 11.4 years at Burlington | Former Burlington Chief Merchandising Officer and long-time Ross/Macy’s merchant. | [S01: FY2026 Proxy Statement, p. 20] |
| President & COO | Travis Marquette | October 2021 | 4.9 years | Former Ross CFO and earlier operations/finance leader; prior Bain, Carter’s and PwC roles. | [S01: FY2026 Proxy Statement, p. 20] |
| EVP & CHRO | Matthew Pasch | September 2023 | 3.0 years in current role; 16.4 years at Burlington | Internal HR leader since 2010. A July 2026 separation agreement set September 1, 2026 as his last day; the provided filing did not name a successor or a reason. | [S01: FY2026 Proxy Statement, p. 20] [S02: Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Exhibit 10.1] |

O’Sullivan is a professional CEO, not a founder or owner-operator. The filing-supported officer group has deep off-price retail experience, particularly from Ross Stores, but the record does not establish a named CHRO successor after Pasch’s scheduled exit.

## 2. Management Stability

| Signal | Detail | Source |

The agreement does not disclose a successor or a cause. This is an Amber succession-continuity item, not evidence of misconduct. | [S02: Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Exhibit 10.1] |

The CEO/CFO pair clears the role-tenure test. The 3.0-year CHRO tenure and planned exit mean the management layer is not churned, but its bench cannot be treated as fully demonstrated until Burlington identifies the replacement and transition plan.

## 3. Stated Strategy & Targets

Management’s strategy is to grow the store base while improving the off-price model: buy more merchandise in season, shift purchases between suppliers and categories as conditions change, and pursue a long-term 2,000-store opportunity. The 2,000-store objective has no stated completion date, so it is an aspiration rather than a target that can yet be scored. [S05: FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1 — Our Off-Price Sourcing and Merchandising Model; Item 1 — Store Expansion and Real Estate Strategy]

For FY2026, after Q2 management guided to 10%–11% total-sales growth, 3%–4% comparable-store-sales growth, about 115 net new stores, 20–40 basis points of Adjusted EBIT-margin expansion, and Adjusted EPS of $11.77–$11.97. These are company-defined non-GAAP targets where stated; they remain untested as of September 29, 2026. [S04: Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Outlook, 2026-08-27]

They nevertheless show targets were published before the measured period and were met or exceeded. The current FY2026 outlook must remain a forecast, not a delivered result.

## 5. Management Read

The CEO/CFO core has been stable for roughly seven and four years respectively, and the completed scorecard has three dated targets that cleared. That supports a strong management-quality read, not an owner-operator conclusion. The biggest open management issue is execution of the CHRO transition: the evidence records Pasch’s exit but no named successor or succession process.
