# Capital-Allocation Scorecard — BURL

Burlington Stores, Inc. is a U.S. GAAP issuer reporting in USD with a January fiscal year-end. This scorecard covers FY2022–FY2025 (fiscal years ended January 28, 2023 through January 31, 2026), with H1 FY2026 shown separately where it updates the assessment. The cross-module quick read and historical-financials report were available and used; upstream `01_management-and-track-record.md` was also available. No multi-year-data cap applies.

## 1. Uses of Capital (3–5 years)

| Use | Cumulative Amount | Currency | % of CFO (or FCF) | Source |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Acquisitions (net) | 0.0 | USD millions | 0.0% of $3,559.9m CFO | No cash acquisitions in the FY2022–FY2025 Capital IQ cash-flow series; no material business acquisition identified in the FY2025 filing. [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025; FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 7—Capital Expenditures, p.33] |
| Buybacks | 1,094.8 | USD millions | 30.8% of CFO | `Repurchase of Common Stock` cash-flow line; this includes program repurchases and may include withholding-related treasury purchases, so it is not identical to the announced-program spend. [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025] |
| Dividends | 0.0 | USD millions | 0.0% of CFO | No dividends paid in the annual cash-flow series. [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025] |
| Capex | 2,880.2 | USD millions | 80.9% of CFO | Cash paid for property and equipment. [FY2024 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.52–53; FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, p.46] |
| Debt repayment | 1,109.0 | USD millions | 31.2% of CFO | Gross long-term debt repayments; debt issuance was also $1,547.9m over the same period. [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025] |

Reported cumulative CFO was $3,559.9m and CFO less cash capex (FCF, cash left after total property investment) was $679.7m across FY2022–FY2025. The listed uses therefore cannot be read as a ranking of FCF alone: capex, repurchases and debt repayment collectively exceeded CFO and were partly funded by debt issuance and cash already on hand. [FY2024 Form 10-K, pp.52–53; FY2025 Form 10-K, p.46; CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025]

## 2. M&A Scorecard

No material M&A in the period. The annual cash-flow series shows no cash-acquisition line in FY2022–FY2025, and the FY2025 filing describes the large investment program as stores, supply chain, IT and a California distribution-centre purchase rather than a business acquisition. This is evidence against a serial-acquirer pattern, not proof that every immaterial asset purchase was absent. [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025; FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 7—Capital Expenditures, p.33]

| Deal | Year | Price | Disclosed Rationale / Synergy | Delivered? | Opportunity Cost (divestitures forced / focus lost / options foregone) | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| No material business acquisition identified | FY2022–FY2025 | 0.0 cash acquisitions reported | Not applicable | Not applicable | No deal-linked divestiture, acquisition synergies, or debt-funded empire-building program was identified. The relevant opportunity cost is instead the $2,880.2m organic capex commitment, whose store- and supply-chain-level returns are not disclosed. | [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025; FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 7—Capital Expenditures, p.33] |

**Serial-acquirer + opportunity-cost test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 4).** No serial-acquirer pattern is proven from the available data, so RF-CAP-004 and its score cap do not apply. The absence of acquisition spending does not itself prove value creation; it removes one common source of value destruction. The principal allocation question is whether the organic investment produces cash and per-share earnings after the expansion cycle.

## 3. Buyback Scorecard

| FY2023 | 243.2 | USD millions | Not disclosed for program purchases | Not determinable | 64.97m to 63.92m (−1.05m) | No on net share-count evidence | No program-price disclosure located | Net share count fell, but price discipline cannot be assessed. | [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow and Balance Sheet, FY2023] |
| FY2024 | 256.3 | USD millions | Not disclosed for program purchases | Not determinable | 63.92m to 63.20m (−0.71m) | No on net share-count evidence | No program-price disclosure located | Net share count fell, but price discipline cannot be assessed. | [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow and Balance Sheet, FY2024] |
| FY2025 | 278.4 cash-flow total; 251.4 announced program | USD millions | 985,594 program shares | $255.1 program spend ÷ shares | 63.20m to 62.69m (−0.52m) | No on net share-count evidence | Announced repurchase amount and shares disclosed; no valuation threshold or price-range analysis disclosed | The program reduced share count; intrinsic-value discipline is not assessable from this module. | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 7—Share Repurchase Program, p.33; CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow and Balance Sheet, FY2025] |
| H1 FY2026 | 167.4 announced program | USD millions | 528,185 program shares | $316.9 program spend ÷ shares | 62.69m to 62.82m (+0.13m) | Not determinable: a convertible-note exchange issued 150,831 shares and other issuance may matter | No valuation threshold or price-range analysis disclosed | The program buyback did not translate into a net first-half reduction; the documented note-exchange issuance is a material offset. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Share Repurchase Program, p.30; Note 4—Long-Term Debt, p.13; cover page] |

The FY2022–FY2025 cash-flow series shows $1,094.8m of gross common-stock repurchases against $96.4m of common-stock issuance, while fully diluted weighted-average shares fell from 65.901m in FY2022 to 64.126m in FY2025 (−2.69%). That supports a net per-share benefit over the completed four-year period, even though stock-based compensation expense totaled $345.7m. It does not establish that every dollar was spent below defensible value. [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow and Income Statement, FY2022–FY2025]

The announced-program average rose from $255.1 in FY2025 to $316.9 in H1 FY2026. That difference is a fact, not a valuation verdict: program timing within each period and a formal valuation threshold are not disclosed. Intrinsic-value discipline not assessable from this module.

## 4. Dividends & Organic Reinvestment

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Payout ratio | 0.0%: no cash dividend paid in FY2022–FY2025 | [CIQ Financials Annual—Cash Flow, FY2022–FY2025] |
| Dividend coverage (FCF) | Not applicable: $0 dividend against cumulative $679.7m CFO-minus-capex FCF | [FY2024 Form 10-K, pp.52–53; FY2025 Form 10-K, p.46] |
| Documented dividend policy exists? Followed for ≥4 years? (A10-01) | Retention policy is stated: Burlington says it intends to retain available funds and future earnings for capex, business initiatives and potential capital-structure initiatives; it does not anticipate a near-term cash dividend. A formal multi-year dividend-payout policy and four years of payments under one are not disclosed. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Dividends, p.30] |
| Incremental ROIC (Δ NOPAT / Δ invested capital) | Approximately 27.9% on a narrow, calculated strict-debt-plus-equity-less-cash basis: NOPAT rose from about $300.6m in FY2022 to $646.2m in FY2025 (+$345.6m); invested capital rose from about $1,398.0m to $2,637.4m (+$1,239.4m). This excludes operating-lease liabilities and is not a company-disclosed project-return measure. CIQ’s differently defined reported return-on-capital series rose from 4.68% to 7.42%, so neither metric proves store- or distribution-centre returns. | [CIQ Financials Annual—Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Ratios, FY2022 and FY2025] |

The two return measures point in the same directional direction but are not interchangeable. The narrow incremental calculation is high because it excludes operating leases and uses balance-sheet financing changes; CIQ’s return-on-capital series remains only 7.42% in FY2025 on its own definition. The conservative conclusion is that organic reinvestment has improved reported returns but is not yet proven at the project level. [CIQ Financials Annual—Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Ratios, FY2022 and FY2025]

## 4A. Distribution Conduct (A10-05)

| Test | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism rationale stated (dividend vs buyback, who benefits)? | Management states that retained funds support capex, business initiatives and potential capital-structure initiatives. It authorizes open-market or privately negotiated buybacks based on market and corporate/regulatory considerations, but does not disclose a valuation threshold or a quantitative dividend-versus-buyback decision rule. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Share Repurchase Program and Dividends, p.30] |
| Promoter participation in any buyback (tender/open-market) | Not applicable to a promoter-tender test: BURL is a U.S. issuer with no promoter class. No tender offer or insider-specific buyback benefit is identified in the supplied materials. | [BURL 2026 DEF 14A, Ownership of Securities, pp.42–43; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2—Share Repurchase Program, p.30] |
| Buyback timing vs promoter pledge / stake changes | Not applicable to promoter pledge; directors and corporate personnel are prohibited from pledging or margining company securities. The policy is not independent proof of compliance. | [BURL 2026 DEF 14A, Prohibition on Hedging and Pledging of Company Stock, pp.57–58] |

## 5. Capital-Allocation Read

**Mixed.** The best completed use is the four-year buyback program: cash repurchases exceeded stock issuance and the fully diluted weighted-average share count fell 2.69%, although H1 FY2026’s program was offset at the outstanding-share level by the note exchange and other issuance. The worst and most consequential use is the $2.88bn capex program: it consumed 80.9% of four-year CFO while reported FCF was only $679.7m, and Burlington does not disclose maintenance-versus-growth capex or project-level returns. No material M&A or debt-funded serial-acquirer pattern is visible; the single biggest capital-allocation signal is therefore whether new stores and supply-chain capacity convert this cash spend into durable per-share returns.

# Incentives & Compensation — BURL

## 1. Compensation Structure

Reporting currency: USD. Period: fiscal 2025, ended January 31, 2026. Amounts below are reported compensation; equity is grant-date fair value, not cash realized.

| Executive | Base | Annual Bonus | Long-Term Incentive | Cash vs Equity Mix | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Michael O'Sullivan, CEO | $1.520m salary | $4.771m annual-incentive payout | $10.843m stock awards: $7.048m PSUs and $3.795m RSUs | $6.307m cash / $10.843m equity = 36.8% / 63.2% of $17.150m total | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 53–55, 61–62] |
| Kristin Wolfe, CFO | $0.882m salary | $1.385m annual-incentive payout | $3.286m stock awards: $2.136m PSUs and $1.150m RSUs | $2.282m cash / $3.286m equity = 41.0% / 59.0% of $5.568m total | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 53–55, 61–62] |

The annual bonus and stock awards made up 91.1% of the CEO's reported fiscal-2025 compensation and 83.9% of the CFO's; these percentages use the Summary Compensation Table's grant-date equity values and are not realized-pay measures. [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, p. 61]

## 2. Performance Metrics

| Plan | Metric | Weight | Per-Share/Returns or Size-Based? | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Fiscal 2025 annual incentive | Adjusted EBIT; $850m target, $923m actual and 157% payout. The committee excluded about $35m of bankruptcy-acquired-lease expense in measuring the result. | 100% of annual-incentive formula | **Size-based / absolute-profit metric.** It rewards operating profit in dollars, not EBIT per share, ROIC, FCF per share, or TSR. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 53–54] |
| Fiscal 2025 LTIP — PSUs | Adjusted EPS growth over fiscal 2025–2027, assessed annually and paid after the three-year period based on the average result. | 65% of annual LTIP grant value | **Per-share.** Adjusted EPS growth is per-share earnings growth, but remains an adjusted measure. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 54–55] |
| Fiscal 2025 LTIP — RSUs | Continued employment; 25% vests on each of four anniversaries. | 35% of annual LTIP grant value | **Neither a returns nor size metric.** It is time-based equity whose realized value moves with BURL's share price. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 54–55, 62] |
| Fiscal 2023 PSU cycle, paid after fiscal 2025 | Adjusted EPS growth; 13.3% target and 20.0% maximum each year. Actual growth was 44%, 35%, and 20% in fiscal 2023–2025, producing a 200% payout. | 100% of that PSU award | **Per-share**, subject to the plan's adjusted-EPS definition. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 47, 55–56] |

The metric mix is not a pure per-share/returns design. The long-term performance award uses per-share Adjusted EPS, but the entire annual cash plan uses absolute Adjusted EBIT and the disclosure does not put a return-on-capital or free-cash-flow-per-share measure into either plan. [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 53–55]

| Pay vs peers (if available) | The independent consultant Meridian and a compensation peer group informed design, but the supplied proxy does not disclose a CEO/CFO peer-median pay figure or percentile. Relative pay magnitude is therefore not assessable from the admitted evidence. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 45, 54] |
| Pay-for-performance alignment | CEO reported total compensation rose at a 10.2% CAGR from fiscal 2022 to fiscal 2025, versus GAAP net income growth of 38.4% over the same interval. That comparison is supportive but not a realized-pay or peer analysis. The fiscal-2025 annual bonus paid 157% after Adjusted EBIT reached $923m versus $850m target. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 53–54, 61, 70] |
| Say-on-pay support (%) | Approximately 89% of votes cast supported the 2025 advisory say-on-pay vote; the roughly 11% opposition is below the 20% significant-dissent threshold in the checklist. | [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 40, 49] |

## 4. Incentive Alignment Read

**Mixed.** Long-term pay has a real per-share element: 65% of the fiscal-2025 LTIP is in three-year Adjusted-EPS PSUs, while 35% is time-vesting equity. But annual cash pay is 100% tied to absolute Adjusted EBIT, and the fiscal-2025 calculation excluded $35m of lease-related expense; there is no ROIC or FCF-per-share measure. The biggest signal is therefore a real but incomplete shift toward per-share rewards, rather than a pay design focused only on per-share value creation. [S1: FY2026 Proxy Statement, pp. 53–55]

Net insider activity: **net selling on the open-market measure** — five sales, zero purchases, and net **−9,231 shares** through the latest open-market event on June 22, 2026. The all-transaction CIQ measure is net **+34,926 shares** through August 5, 2026, but it includes grants, exercises, issuer/tax-withholding transactions and other non-market legs; it is not evidence of net cash buying. [CIQ Public Ownership → Insider Trading, `insider_open_market` and `insider_net_activity` facts, through 2026-06-22 and 2026-08-05]

The May 4 Marquette open-market sale preceded the May 28 Q1 release, but that release reported 14% sales growth, 6% comparable-store growth and adjusted EPS of $2.10, above guidance. The available evidence therefore does not establish insider selling ahead of weak results. [BURL Q1 FY2026 earnings release, 2026-05-28]

## 5. Blunt Read

Management has 1.3% beneficial ownership, but the disclosed total includes options and RSUs, and no open-market purchases appear in the last 12 months. The cleaner behavior signal is five open-market sales totaling 9,231 shares; it is modest relative to 62.8m shares outstanding and is not evidenced as sales ahead of weak results. The main positive is control fairness: no controller, one vote per share, and no disclosed pledging; the main limitation is that the filing does not establish how much insider stock was bought with cash rather than received through compensation.

# Board & Shareholder Rights — BURL

**Scope and timing.** This is a U.S./NYSE governance read. The most recent proxy in the frozen pool is dated April 2, 2026 and describes a 12-member board before the May 19 annual meeting; it says Mary Ann Tocio would not stand for re-election and the board would then fall to 11. No post-meeting Form 8-K or revised board roster is in the admitted pool, so the tables label this as the proxy-date snapshot rather than inventing a September composition. [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 3–4, 11]

## 1. Board Composition

| Feature | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Board size | 12 at the April 2 proxy date; the proxy states that Tocio's May 19 retirement would reduce it to 11. | [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 4, 11] |
| Independent directors (%) — vs the applicable floor | 11 of 12, or 91.7%, are NYSE-independent; O'Sullivan is the CEO and the sole non-independent director. This clears the U.S. listing floor and the module's ≥50% Green band. | [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 3–4, 24] |
| Chair / CEO split? Chair non-executive, non-promoter? Designated (not rotating)? | Split. John Mahoney has been independent chair since February 2020; Michael O'Sullivan is CEO. The board elects the chair annually, so the chair is designated but not permanent. | [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 21–22] |
| Woman director / independent woman director where mandated | Four of the 12 proxy-date directors are women—Goodman, Rodriguez, Sen and Tocio—and all are shown as independent. The post-retirement count is not evidenced in the admitted pool. | [FY2026 DEF 14A, p. 4] |
| Meeting count, longest gap, ID present in every quorum (A1-14) | Four board meetings in FY2025; every director attended at least 92% of board and assigned-committee meetings. The filing does not disclose the longest gap or an independent-director quorum for each meeting. | [FY2026 DEF 14A, p. 24] |
| Audit / Comp (NRC) / Nominating committee independence | Audit: five NYSE/SEC-independent members, all financial experts, eight meetings. Compensation: three independent members, four meetings. NCGC: four independent members, four meetings. | [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 24, 32–34] |

\*Tocio was a proxy-date director but was due to retire at the May 19, 2026 annual meeting.

The legal-independence statistic is favorable, but the true-independence test is not. Five of 11 legally independent directors at the proxy date—Hitch, Mahoney, McNamara, Sullivan and Tocio—had served more than 10 years. Tocio's planned departure would reduce that count to four, still above the Registry's Red threshold of two. This is a tenure signal, not evidence that any director has a conflicted transaction or failed the `07` integrity screen. [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 4, 11–17, 24; 07, Person Register]

## 3. Related-Party Transactions & Group Leakage

No material related-party transactions were disclosed under Item 404 from the start of FY2025 through the proxy date. The proxy says directors and officers provide information for the related-party review and that the Audit Committee approves transactions subject to the policy. This is evidence of approval design and of no Item 404-reportable transaction; it is not a substitute for `09`'s item-level A5 quantification or proof that no transaction exists under every accounting definition. ## 5. Minority-Shareholder Protection Read

**Adequate.** The board has a 91.7% legal-independence ratio, an independent chair, fully independent standing committees, majority voting in uncontested elections and proxy access. [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 3–4, 21, 24, 32–34]

The main counterweight is true independence: five proxy-date independent directors had served more than 10 years, meeting the Registry's Red threshold even though none was given a Material or Disqualifying `07` grade. Minority holders also cannot call a special meeting or act by written consent, and the phased declassification and 75% removal hurdle remain until the 2027 annual meeting. [FY2026 DEF 14A, pp. 11, 21, 24; FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1A, p. 17; 07, Person Register]

# Candor & Disclosure Quality — BURL

## 1. Owning the Misses

The completed promise-versus-delivery tests supplied by `01_management-and-track-record` contain no management miss: FY2025 Adjusted EBIT exceeded its target, the FY2023–FY2025 PSU Adjusted EPS targets cleared their maximum payout, and Q2 FY2026 was within or above the Q1 guide. The current Q3 FY2026 EPS outlook is lower than last year's $1.80, but it is forward guidance, not an actual miss; management attributes the planned decline to the quantified reinvestment of tariff refunds. [S01: Management & Track Record, §4] [S03: Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Outlook]

| Miss (from 01) | How It Was Communicated | Owned or Obscured? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| No completed management miss identified in the supplied delivery record | Not applicable. The closest current adverse comparison is Q3 FY2026 Adjusted EPS guidance of $1.60–$1.70 versus $1.80 a year earlier; the release explicitly attributes the margin and EPS effect to the planned reinvestment of approximately 40% of the $55m tariff refund in Q3 and 60% in Q4. | Not assessable as an owning-the-miss test; this is a disclosed forecast choice, not a delivered miss. | [S01: Management & Track Record, §4] [S03: Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Outlook] |

## 2. Non-GAAP / Adjustment Aggressiveness

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring "one-off" addbacks | FY2025 adjusted earnings excluded net favourable lease costs of $7.7m, impairment of $9.9m and litigation of $4.2m. Each category also appeared in FY2023 and FY2024, so these should not be described as wholly one-off. | [S02: FY2025 Form 10-K, Results of Operations—non-GAAP reconciliation] [S07: Earnings Quality, §§4–5] |
| GAAP-to-adjusted gap (magnitude / trend) | FY2025 GAAP net income was $610.2m and Adjusted Net Income was $625.7m: a $15.5m, 2.5% gap. Q2 FY2026 is different in direction: Adjusted EPS of $2.37 explicitly removes the $0.64-per-share tariff-refund benefit as well as lease costs, while GAAP EPS was $2.88. | [S02: FY2025 Form 10-K, Results of Operations—non-GAAP reconciliation] [S03: Q2 FY2026 earnings release, pp. 1–2 and Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures] [S07: Earnings Quality, §7] |
| Does adjusted framing flatter reality? | Partly. The recurring exclusions make adjusted results less conservative than GAAP in FY2025, but the magnitude is modest and the Q2 presentation removes, rather than keeps, the large $55m positive tariff refund. The company provides historical reconciliations, while forward Adjusted EBIT/EPS have no quantitative GAAP reconciliation because it says the required estimates are inherently difficult to predict. | [S02: FY2025 Form 10-K, Results of Operations—non-GAAP reconciliation] [S03: Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Outlook and Note Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures] |

## 3. Disclosure Transparency

Burlington reports one consolidated operating segment, so it cannot provide separate segment economics; its FY2025 10-K nevertheless identifies net income, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBIT, comparable-store sales, gross margin, inventory and liquidity as key measures, and the Q2 call gave the tariff-refund amount, reinvestment timing, inventory mix, store count and operating drivers. [S02: FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 2—Segment Information; Results of Operations] [S05: Q2 FY2026 earnings call, prepared remarks]

The same principal KPI set is visible across FY2022–FY2025 annual disclosures and the Q1/Q2 FY2026 calls, and no KPI was identified as redefined or dropped after deterioration. The evidence does not demonstrate the five full years needed for the A7-03 Green band, and category- or region-level profitability is not disclosed; the latter is a limitation of a one-segment issuer, not evidence of a transparency reduction. [S06: FY2024 Annual Report, MD&A—Key performance and non-GAAP measures] [S02: FY2025 Form 10-K, Results of Operations] [S04: Q1 FY2026 earnings call, prepared remarks] [S05: Q2 FY2026 earnings call, prepared remarks and Q&A]

## 4. Tone in Bad Times

The two supplied verbatim calls cover quarters that beat guidance; the closest recent stress test is the Q3 FY2026 guide, where management set out the lower $1.60–$1.70 Adjusted EPS range, the 60–80bp operating-margin decline, the 40%/60% tariff-refund reinvestment split, and the weather and consumer risks rather than calling the impact immaterial. [S03: Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Outlook] [S05: Q2 FY2026 earnings call, prepared remarks]

In Q&A, management answered directly on tariff-refund uncertainty, cannibalisation, weather exposure, consumer pressure and the trade-off between sales and margin. The language is promotional in a good quarter (for example, calling underlying momentum “extremely robust”), but the numerical disclosures and direct risk answers mean no evasiveness was identified; a real delivered bad-quarter transcript is not in the admitted record. [S04: Q1 FY2026 earnings call, Q&A] [S05: Q2 FY2026 earnings call, Q&A]

## 5. Candor Read

**Mixed.** Management was specific about the $55m tariff refund, removed it from its underlying-Q2 presentation, and explained why it lowered Q3 margin and EPS while keeping the full-year effect neutral. The counterweight is recurring exclusions labelled non-GAAP adjustments and no actual management miss or bad-result call in the available sample, so the evidence does not support a candid / high-trust conclusion.

The single biggest candor signal is the explicit treatment of the tariff refund: $55m received in Q2, about 40% to be reinvested in Q3 and 60% in Q4, with a stated neutral full-year impact. The recurring lease-cost, impairment and litigation exclusions are a medium-severity caution, not evidence that the Q2 result was concealed.

RF-DISC-002 (recurring "one-off" / aggressive non-GAAP add-backs)

## 3B. Lineage & Phoenix Read (A17-02, A17-03)

The documents support a disclosed continuity story: first BCF store in 1972, BCFWC New Jersey organization/reincorporation, Bain's 2006 acquisition, IPO in 2013, and later Burlington branding. [BURL Investors, “Our History”, accessed 2026-09-29; BURL 2015 DEF 14A, corporate history] No filing or public source in the admitted evidence shows that an entity failed, that assets were shifted from an insolvent predecessor, or that a creditor-avoidance phoenix occurred. The business, brands and address continuity are therefore explained by disclosed group history, though the predecessor/former-name legal sweep belongs to `12` and remains pending that handoff.

## 6. Provenance & Next Data Request

The filing supplied 43 subjects and the discovery work added four (the former legal name, BCFWC lineage, BCF Direct and founder Milstein); no subject was user supplied. Independent directors are excluded from beneficial-interest analysis only; their individual integrity coverage remains in Section 1. The unresolved aggregator conflict is `Burlington Coat Factory Investment Holdings, Inc.` (Exhibit 21) versus CIQ's similar plural spelling/former-name claim. **Single highest-value next data request:** an identifier-linked paid U.S. people-and-entity registry/court/sanctions batch for the 40-person roster and BCFWC/BCF Direct, including historical officer roles and state case dockets.

## 7. People & Network Integrity Read

No person or scoped entity has an attributed Material or Disqualifying fact in the admitted evidence. The only decision-relevant network fact is a disclosed historic BCFWC lineage that explains the company’s 1972 history and trademark ownership; it is not a phoenix read. The riskiest unresolved point is not a red flag but coverage: the roster lacks unique officer IDs and the complete registry/court/global-list sweep could not run. A rational minority holder should treat the current integrity read as **PASS, coverage-limited**, with the People & Network Integrity Score capped at 65 until the missing primary screens and the `12` lineage handoff are complete.

## 3. Calibre, Rotation & Regulator Discipline (A4-01, A4-02, A4-13)

| Test | Raw value | Green band | Red band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A4-01 — tenure vs local cap; rotation real? | Deloitte has audited BURL since 1983 (43 years). BURL says Deloitte rotates the lead engagement partner every five years and the Audit Committee interviews/selects the candidate; actual partner names and rotation dates are not disclosed. | U.S. lead-partner rotation is orderly and real | Same-network affiliate swap, or cap dodged via loopholes | Amber — no U.S. firm cap is breached, but 43-year firm tenure makes the undisclosed implementation of partner rotation material to independence. There is no outgoing/incoming firm because no firm change occurred. | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, p. 41]; [FY2026 DEF 14A, Proposal 2, p. 37] |
| A4-02 — firm calibre vs company complexity | Deloitte is a Big Four PCAOB-registered annual firm. The PCAOB's firm record lists Deloitte disciplinary proceedings in 2007, 2013 and 2018; the 2018 order censured Deloitte and imposed a $500,000 penalty over unrelated Jack Henry audits. | Big-4 / peer-reviewed national firm, listed practice sized to this company | Firm too small for complexity, or firm/partner with disciplinary history | Red — capacity is not in doubt, but the strict disciplinary-history band is met. The order concerns another issuer and does not establish a BURL audit error. | [PCAOB Firm Summary for Deloitte & Touche LLP, queried 2026-09-29]; [PCAOB Release 105-2018-008, pp. 1–3] |
| A4-13 — PCAOB / SEC orders vs firm or signing partner | Deloitte is currently PCAOB-registered, but the PCAOB record lists firm proceedings in 2007, 2013 and 2018. The current BURL signing partner is not identified, so a partner-specific sweep could not run. | No orders against firm or signing partner | Active order or debarment (also RF-AUD-007) | Red — historical final firm orders mean “no orders” cannot be claimed. Current PCAOB registration is evidence against a present firm debarment, not evidence that historical orders did not occur. Partner coverage is limited. | [PCAOB Firm Summary for Deloitte & Touche LLP, queried 2026-09-29]; [PCAOB Release 105-2018-008, pp. 1–3]; [PCAOB Release 105-2013-008, 2013-10-22] |

The PCAOB 2018 order found that Deloitte's work on an unrelated issuer's FY2012–FY2014 audits did not obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to support opinions and led to a $500,000 penalty. The PCAOB firm register nevertheless shows Deloitte as currently registered. This is a firm-quality and diligence finding, not a claim that BURL's financial statements are misstated. [PCAOB Release 105-2018-008, pp. 1–3; PCAOB Firm Summary for Deloitte & Touche LLP, queried 2026-09-29]

## 10. Read

BURL's assurance is **mixed — watch the named link**. Deloitte issued clean consolidated opinions for the last three reported years and an unqualified FY2025 ICFR opinion, while disclosed non-audit fees were only 5.7% of audit fees in FY2025. The weakest link is not a modified BURL opinion; it is the combination of a 43-year audit-firm tenure, historical PCAOB discipline of Deloitte, no current signing-partner identification, and no disclosed component-auditor coverage. Trust would increase with the current BURL Form AP/partner record, a partner-specific discipline sweep, and an Audit Committee disclosure of Deloitte's principal/component coverage plus all network-firm fees.

# Related-Party & Group Forensics — BURL

## 1. RPT Intensity & the Applicable Regime (A5-01)

BURL is a U.S. issuer. The applicable screen for each fiscal year is SEC Regulation S-K Item 404(a): a transaction exceeding $120,000 in which a related person has a direct or indirect material interest must be disclosed. This is a disclosure threshold, not a measure of every de-minimis consolidated intercompany transaction. The current proxy covers the period from the beginning of FY2025 through April 2, 2026; the frozen pool does not contain the corresponding FY2023 or FY2024 proxy disclosures. [FY2026 Proxy Statement, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions]

| FY | Aggregate RPTs ex-dividends | % of revenue | % of PAT | % of assets | Material-RPT line that year | Above the line? | Minority-approved? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | Not assessable — no contemporaneous Item 404 disclosure in the frozen pool | N/A | N/A | N/A | Item 404(a): $120k | Not assessable | Not assessable | Insufficient Data | [FY2024 Form 10-K, Schedule I; frozen-pool inventory, 2026-09-29] |
| FY2024 | Not assessable — no contemporaneous Item 404 disclosure in the frozen pool | N/A | N/A | N/A | Item 404(a): $120k | Not assessable | Not assessable | Insufficient Data | [FY2024 Form 10-K, Schedule I; frozen-pool inventory, 2026-09-29] |
| FY2025 (ended 2026-01-31) | $0 of Item-404-reportable related-person transactions; the proxy does not quantify every non-reportable consolidated intercompany flow | 0.0% of $11,549.6m | 0.0% of $610.2m | 0.0% of $9,919.1m | Item 404(a): $120k | No reported transaction above the line | Not required on the disclosed $0 category | Amber — current reportable screen clear; full aggregate RPT total is not disclosed | [FY2026 Proxy Statement, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions; FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income and Balance Sheets; earnings/01, Annual Financial Table] |

The disclosed Item 404 category is $0 / $11,549.6m revenue = 0.0% and $0 / $10,700.7m operating-cost/expense base = 0.0%. It is below the 25% test, but that hard-lock conclusion belongs to `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`; this report does not re-adjudicate it. The result does not prove that de-minimis or consolidated intercompany transactions were zero. [business-model/01_disqualifier-scan, Disqualifier 3; FY2026 Proxy Statement, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions]

## 2. The RPT Ledger (every named counterparty)

The proxy names no Item-404-reportable related-person counterparty. The only named group financing channel found in the filed parent-only schedules is the joint BCFWC/Burlington Merchandising obligation below; it is eliminated in consolidation and is not a payment to a promoter or a separate controller.

| Counterparty | Relationship | Type (sales/purchases/royalty/rent/loan/guarantee/other) | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 (latest) | Trend | Arm's-length basis disclosed? | Source |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Burlington Coat Factory Warehouse Corporation (BCFWC) and Burlington Merchandising Corporation (BMC), jointly and severally | Wholly owned subsidiaries | Parent intercompany note receivable supporting the Parent's convertible notes | $453.2m joint amount | $453.2m joint amount | $297.1m joint amount | Down $156.1m (34.4%) from FY2024; do not add the joint amount twice | Terms and interest rate stated as consistent with the Parent's 2025/2027 convertible notes; no separate third-party pricing study disclosed | [FY2024 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 4; FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 4] |

There is no disclosed external promoter, executive, director, or >5% holder on the other side of this joint note. The history is therefore a disclosed intra-group funding flow, not evidence that value moved to a controller. Its size still warrants an Amber, rather than a Green, group-topology read. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Schedule I, Note 4; FY2026 Proxy Statement, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions]

Neither BCFWC nor BMC appears as both an external customer and vendor in the filed RPT record; no customer/vendor pair can be price-matched because no external RPT values were disclosed.

No both-role lead exists in the disclosed RPT data, so there is no circularity evidence and no round-tripping red flag. This is not a clearance of ordinary suppliers, which are outside Item 404 unless a related-person link exists.

## 14. Read

No currently reportable value transfer to a promoter, executive, director, or >5% holder was disclosed: the FY2025 Item 404 category is $0, or 0.0% of reported revenue and PAT. The largest named group channel is the $297.1m BCFWC/BMC joint intercompany note, down from $453.2m, with terms matching the Parent's convertible notes; it is a material internal funding flow, not proven minority leakage. The structure has 25 named subsidiaries and almost all reported cash sits below the Parent, but disclosed $409.0m FY2025 upstream contributions argue against a demonstrated trapped-cash loop; no entity-level cash map or ownership tree is supplied. The single highest-value disclosure would be a legal-entity chart with cash, debt, guarantees, and intercompany balances by material subsidiary, plus prior-year Item 404 transaction schedules.

# Contingent Liabilities & Commitments — BURL

**Scope and evidence limit.** Burlington Stores, Inc. is a U.S. GAAP reporter with a January fiscal year-end; amounts are USD millions unless stated otherwise. The frozen pool supplies three comparable fiscal-year observations for letters of credit (FY2023–FY2025) and a current Q2 FY2026 update, rather than five annual reports. `balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md` is not present inside this continuation root, so this report proceeds from the frozen filing pool and does not recompute a survival-module result. No web/database posture sweep was run: the filings do not name or quantify individual disputes that could be searched without guessing, so all litigation-posture statements below are filings-only.

## 1. Headline Exposure (A7a-01)

| Measure | Amount | Denominator (figure + source) | % | Band (Green <5% NW / Red >25% NW or >50% PAT) | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Quantified contingent liability — letters of credit arrangements | $58.0 | Net worth = $2,002.248 [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.5] | 2.90% | Green on net-worth test | Green | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Commitments and Contingencies, p.20] |
| Quantified contingent liability — letters of credit arrangements | $58.0 | FY2025 PAT / net income = $610.153 [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income, p.43] | 9.51% | Green on PAT test (<50%) | Green | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Commitments and Contingencies, p.20] |
| Total commitments (separate line): inventory purchases for goods not received | $2,558.5 | Net worth = $2,002.248 [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.5] | 127.78% | Not a contingent-liability band; must not be added to the $58.0m CL total | Amber | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 — Purchase Commitments, p.20] |

The $58.0m figure is the only quantified current contingent obligation in the note. It is not a complete estimate of all legal exposure: the filing describes litigation and regulatory proceedings but provides neither a monetary range nor a provision by matter. The $2,558.5m merchandise-purchase commitment is contractually important and larger than equity, but it would deliver inventory rather than represent a stand-alone contingent loss; it is therefore shown separately, not combined with CLs.

The item-level record does **not** show a hidden worsening inside a flat letter-of-credit total: annual LC arrangements fell from $75.8m to $50.4m before the current $58.0m increase. The legal bucket has no amount or docket-level posture, however, so it cannot be treated as clean merely because no total is printed. No silent disappearance or repeated crystallization was identified in the disclosed LC or tax-benefit roll-forwards; RF-CL-003 is not triggered from the available evidence.

## 11. Read

Burlington’s quantified current contingent obligation is $58.0m of letters of credit, only 2.90% of $2,002.248m of stockholders’ equity and 9.51% of FY2025 PAT of $610.153m. The largest disclosed contractual commitment is instead $2,558.5m of goods not yet received—127.78% of equity—which should be monitored as inventory-buying exposure, not folded into the CL total as though it were a loss. Tax provisions are explicitly recognized and the gross unrecognized-tax-benefit balance fell from $3.132m to $1.566m over two years; the real disclosure limit is that legal, regulatory, group-guarantee, recourse-financing and FX exposures are not quantified or separated. A rational minority holder should watch whether the current Q2 increase in LC arrangements and inventory commitments turns into higher working-capital strain, and request case-level amounts, provisions and outcomes if any legal matter becomes material.

## 2. Beneish M-Score (A8-14) — computed with python3, computation shown

The M-score is a statement-pattern screen, not proof of fraud. I computed the mandated formula from Section 1 using the Bash/Python method.

| Component | Value FY2025 | Non-manipulator mean | Manipulator zone | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| DSRI (receivables outrunning sales) | 1.0989 | 1.031 | ≥1.465 | Green |
| GMI (gross margin deteriorating) | 0.9866 | 1.014 | ≥1.193 | Green |
| AQI (asset quality softening) | 0.9338 | 1.039 | ≥1.254 | Green |
| SGI (sales growth pressure) | 1.0879 | 1.134 | ≥1.607 | Green |
| DEPI (depreciation rate slowing) | 1.0965 | 1.001 | ≥1.077 | Amber — one zone component |
| SGAI (overhead vs sales) | 0.9893 | 1.054 | not banded | Green |
| LVGI (leverage rising) | 0.9882 | 1.037 | ≥1.111 | Green |
| TATA (accruals vs assets) | −0.0626 | 0.018 | ≥0.031 | Green |

Composite: M = −4.84 + 0.920×1.0989 + 0.528×0.9866 + 0.404×0.9338 + 0.892×1.0879 + 0.115×1.0965 − 0.172×0.9893 − 0.327×0.9882 + 4.679×(−0.0626) = **−2.6207**. [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp. 43, 45–46]; computation by this agent.

| Composite / rule | Value | Green band | Amber band | Red band | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| M-score | −2.6207 | < −2.22, no component in zone | −2.22 to −1.78 | > −1.78 | Amber: composite Green, but one zone component must be Amber. |
| Components in manipulator zone | 1 of 7 | 0 | 1–2 | ≥3 | Amber |

DEPI is the only zone signal: the depreciation rate fell from 12.79% to 11.67%. PP&E grew 33.5% and D&A rose 20.2%, so the filings do not establish an unexplained expense suppression. [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp. 45–46, 62]

## 3. Dechow F-Score & Accrual Battery (A8-17, A8-18) — computed with python3, computation shown

The Dechow F-score estimates misstatement probability; 1.00 is the average company. RSST is total accruals, or profit booked before cash, across working capital, non-current operating assets and financing. Soft assets are assets other than cash and PP&E, which rely more on estimates.

| Test | Value | Green band | Red band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Dechow F-score | 0.8819 | <1.00 | ≥1.85; ≥2.45 high | Green | Required Python computation. |
| RSST accruals / average assets | 2.13% | ≤3% | ≥10% | Green | ΔWC −172.098 + ΔNCO 742.551 + ΔFIN −371.517 = 198.936; average assets 9,344.735. |
| Soft assets / total assets | 55.67% | <50% | >65% and rising | Amber | (9,919.057 − 3,164.218 − 1,232.525) / 9,919.057. |
| Δ receivables / average assets | 0.18% | <2% | ≥5% | Green | 17.217 / 9,344.735. |
| Δ inventory / average assets | 0.65% | <2% | ≥5% | Green | 61.128 / 9,344.735. |
| A8-18 — issuance in a flagged year | $500.0m Term B-7 incremental loans; F 0.8819 and TATA −6.26% | none while flagged | issued while F ≥1.85 or TATA ≥3.1% | Green | Debt was raised, but not in a battery-flagged year. |

Inputs and output: WC FY2023/FY2024/FY2025 = −613.418/−467.515/−639.613; NCO = 2,093.636/2,554.122/3,296.673; FIN = −1,408.645/−1,710.809/−2,082.326. Cash sales rose from 10,603.025 to 11,532.390, or 8.765%; ROA rose 6.113% to 6.529%. The Python output was pred = −5.7219, probability = 0.3263%, F = 0.8819. [FY2024 Form 10-K, pp. 50, 52–53]; [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp. 43, 45–46]

## 12. Forensics Read

BURL’s measured batteries do not show a current manipulation pattern: Beneish M = **−2.6207** and Dechow F = **0.8819**, both below Red cutoffs. The worst measured signal is DEPI of **1.0965**, which can rhyme with delayed depreciation, but PP&E grew 33.5% and D&A rose 20.2%, so the filings do not establish expense suppression. CFO/PAT of **2.02×**, CFO/EBITDA of **99.2%**, and collections growth of 8.77% corroborate earnings; cash taxes were nearly flat and require a timing check. Cash authenticity is **not proven from available data** because interest income is scope-mixed and the public audit report does not disclose bank-confirmation procedures. A minority holder has no measured books-manipulation red flag today, but should require FY2026 detail on cash interest, receivable ageing and capitalised-development additions.

# Regulatory, Legal & Compliance — BURL

**As of:** 2026-09-29. **Scope:** Burlington Stores, Inc. (NYSE: BURL; CIK 0001579298; Delaware). This is a coverage-limited company-level public-record sweep, not a finding that the record is clear. The independent databases available in this run did identify court and agency records; several complete issuer-search interfaces, the NYSE issuer-fine history, and full rating-action histories were unavailable. Accordingly, the Legal & Regulatory Risk Score is floored at 40/100 (inverted — higher is worse) and confidence is capped at 70.

## 9. Read

**Hygiene lapses, watch.** The public record adds a court-approved $5.2m wage settlement and an active, unquantified commercial case; the filings disclose both categories but not the case names or known settlement amount. The known settlement is below the module’s materiality threshold, so there is no demonstrated material undisclosed matter or regulator-enforcement cap. The anonymous hotline is real, but the lack of a named ombudsperson and complaint statistics means its effectiveness is not proven; incomplete regulator, exchange, sanctions, court and ratings coverage keeps risk at the 40 floor rather than calling the record clean.

# Valuation Module — BURL (Synthesis)

## Abstract

BURL is fairly valued: the $254.69 close is 7.5% above the $237.01 base value, so there is no cushion. The 12-month levels are $370.63 bull, $237.01 base, and $66.31 cyclical-trough bear; a 70% peer forward-earnings / 30% discounted-cash-flow blend drives the base. At today's price, the model implies annual free-cash-flow growth of 46.75% through FY2030 or a 13.85% operating-profit margin, neither proven by current evidence. The bear level implies 74.0% downside, while valid methods span $133.46–$302.88 and cap confidence. Verdict: fairly valued because the base is 7.5% below the price, but the outcome range is wide. [Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §§2–5; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2–6]

## 1. Valuation Verdict

- **Verdict:** **Fairly valued** — the $254.69 price is 7.46% above the $237.01 base fair value, within the module's ±10% band. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§4 and 6]
- **Base-case fair value (point, per share):** **$237.01**, on a 12-month horizon. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2–3]
- **Current price:** **$254.69**, pool-verified NYSE close on 2026-09-28; one trading day old. [Capital IQ Comps, Financial Data, subject row, 2026-09-28; CIQ facts sidecar]
- **Bull / Base / Bear fair-value levels (points):** **$370.63 / $237.01 / $66.31** per share; the bear is a recoverable cyclical-trough case, not a permanent-impairment case. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §3]
- **Cross-method dispersion (football field, low–high):** **$133.46–$302.88**, a 126.94% high-to-low spread measured from the low; excluded own-history sensitivities were $317.03–$438.53. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§1–2]
- **Valuation attractiveness /100** *(higher = cheaper)*: **40** — the base implies 6.94% downside from price, although the peer method alone implies 10.5% upside. [Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §5; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2 and 4]
- **Margin of safety /100** *(higher = better)*: **30** — margin of safety, meaning the price discount to base fair value, is **(7.46%)**, so no cushion exists. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §4]
- **Valuation confidence /100:** **50** — data coverage is good, but the 126.94% method spread triggers a hard maximum of 55. [Valuation 00 Data Triage, §§3–6; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§1–2]
- **Downside risk /100** *(higher = worse; inverted)*: **88** — downside to the $66.31 bear value is **73.96%**. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§3–4]
- **Data quality /100:** **88** — all core inputs are present and the price is fresh, but the enterprise-value vendor series does not reconcile and the fully diluted share count is a period-average proxy. [Valuation 00 Data Triage, §§3–6; Valuation 01 Price & Capital Structure, §§2 and 4; Valuation 02 Own History, §1]
- **Overall usefulness /100:** **78** — the module produces testable fair-value levels and a price-implied expectations read, but its base value remains sensitive to a large peer-versus-cash-flow disagreement. [Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §5; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2–6]
- **Dominant valuation method:** Matched peer NTM P/E — next-twelve-month price divided by earnings — at 70% weight, because it uses direct off-price peers and avoids the lease-sensitive enterprise-value bridge; the applied 23.333x multiple retains a 10% discount to the direct-peer median. [Capital IQ Comps, Financial Data and Trading Multiples, as of 2026-09-28; Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §§4–5]
- **What's priced in:** The reverse-DCF, which solves what the current price assumes, requires **46.75% annual FCFF growth** through FY2030 to $1.641bn, or a **13.85% EBIT margin**; FCFF is cash available to debt and equity providers, and EBIT is operating profit before interest and tax. Neither requirement is proven. [Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §§2–5]
- **Biggest valuation risk:** Store and supply-chain spending may not turn earnings growth into durable cash flow; that is the main reason the DCF is $133.46 while the peer base is $281.39. [Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§2 and 6–8; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §2]

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** The filing-based DCF is **$133.46**, 47.6% below the current price, and the same model requires 46.75% annual FCFF growth or a 13.85% EBIT margin to justify $254.69, versus a 7.8% LTM EBIT margin. [Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§6–8; Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §§2–5]
- **Strongest bull point:** A 10% warranted discount to the two direct peers still gives **$281.39** on NTM P/E, 10.5% above price; the bull reaches **$370.63** only with $13.00 NTM EPS and a 28.51x P/E. [Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §§4–5; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §3]
- **Single killer risk:** The peer method values forward earnings, while the DCF exposes weak cash conversion under heavy capital spending; if growth capex does not fall or generate later cash flow, the peer-led base is too high. [Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§2 and 4–8]
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** The $281.39 peer value contradicts the below-market $237.01 blended base, while the $133.46 DCF contradicts the peer read; the 126.94% field shows that neither direction is independently settled. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§1–2]

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| valuation-data-triage | **Sufficient; no active partial-data cap.** | A fresh pool price, forward estimates, peers, cash flow and capital structure are all present; SOTP is inapplicable because BURL has one reportable segment. [Valuation 00 Data Triage, §§3–6] |
| price-and-capital-structure | **Pool-verified anchor available.** | Price is $254.69; canonical strict net debt is $1.216bn and EV is $17.210bn, while CIQ's $5.202bn net debt is a separately reconciled lease-inclusive vendor measure. [Valuation 01 Price & Capital Structure, §§1 and 4–7] |
| multiples-own-history | **De-rated, but reversion is not an admissible base.** | Mechanical median values are $317.03 on EV/Sales and $438.53 on P/E, but the vendor EV basis and historical share basis do not reconcile cleanly. [Valuation 02 Own History, §§3–6] |
| relative-valuation-peers | **The peer gap is wider than warranted after a 10% durability discount.** | Matched NTM P/E gives $281.39; the $302.88 EV/EBITDA check depends on a lease-inclusive vendor bridge. [Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §§4–7] |
| intrinsic-dcf | **Intrinsic value is $133.46 per share.** | The sensitivity range is $109.91–$168.23 and terminal value supplies 74.35% of EV, leaving the result sensitive to capex and later cash conversion. [Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§5–8] |
| reverse-dcf | **Current expectations are aggressive and not proven.** | Price requires 46.75% annual FCFF growth through FY2030 or a 13.85% steady-state EBIT margin; holding the DCF cash path fixed instead implies a 6.95% discount rate. [Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §§2–5] |
| sum-of-the-parts | **Single-segment — SOTP collapses.** | BURL's one U.S. off-price retail segment accounts for 100% of reportable revenue and profit, so a breakup would duplicate the peer method. [Valuation 06 Sum-of-the-Parts, §§1–5] |
| scenario-and-fair-value | **$370.63 bull / $237.01 base / $66.31 cyclical-trough bear.** | The 70% peer / 30% DCF base is 6.94% below price, with a negative 7.46% margin of safety and 73.96% downside to bear. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2–6] |

## 3. Reconciliation

The valid football field runs from the **$133.46 DCF** to the **$302.88 peer EV/EBITDA support check**, a 126.94% high-to-low spread; this exceeds 40%, so it is the first finding and caps confidence at 55. The direct comparison between method base points is also wide: $133.46 for DCF versus $281.39 for peer NTM P/E. Own-history sensitivities of $317.03–$438.53 remain visible but receive no weight because their historical share and enterprise-value bases do not reconcile; SOTP adds no value because the company has one segment. [Valuation 02 Own History, §§1 and 4–6; Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §5; Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§6–8; Valuation 06 Sum-of-the-Parts, §5; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§1–2]

The reconciled base is **$237.01**, calculated as `70% × $281.39 peer value + 30% × $133.46 DCF`. The peer method leads because it uses BURL's $12.06 NTM EPS and a 23.333x warranted P/E against Ross and TJX, while avoiding the inconsistent lease treatment in EV multiples. The DCF remains a material cross-check because its $850.5m FY2030 FCFF path is already growth-heavy, yet the price requires $1.641bn under the same WACC and terminal-growth convention. [Capital IQ Comps, Financial Data and Trading Multiples, as of 2026-09-28; Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §5; Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §4; Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §2; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §2]

**Sector Cycle Reality Test roll-up:** `02` and `03` both found the test **Not assessable — no sector-level multiple history**. Neither called its reference cycle-elevated or cycle-depressed, neither emitted `RF-VAL-001` or `RF-VAL-002`, and there is no same-direction compounding cap. The absence still matters: BURL's old multiple band and today's peer median cannot be treated as stable, independent anchors. [Valuation 02 Own History, §5; Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §6]

The pool price is one trading day old, so the separate stale-price cap does not apply. [Valuation 01 Price & Capital Structure, §§1 and 7]

## 5. Fair-Value Summary

The 12-month levels are **$370.63 bull, $237.01 base, and $66.31 cyclical-trough bear**; the 70%-weighted peer NTM P/E drives the base, while the 30%-weighted DCF forces a cash-conversion discount. At $254.69, the reverse-DCF implies 46.75% annual FCFF growth through FY2030 or a 13.85% EBIT margin, neither established by the earnings or business-model evidence. Margin of safety is **(7.46%)**, meaning price is above base fair value, while downside to the $66.31 bear is a separate **73.96%** loss measure. There is no controlling-owner value-trap flag, but there is multiple-reversion risk: BURL's 42/100 business quality, narrow and not yet economically proven moat, capital needs, and unavailable sector-multiple history do not justify simply restoring the old P/E band. The matched peer P/E is the method to trust most; the DCF is the necessary downside check, while own-history reversion and SOTP should receive no weight. [Business Model 07 Business Quality, §§1–4; Business Model 09 Moat, §§3–5; Valuation 02 Own History, §§4–6; Valuation 03 Relative Valuation, §§4–7; Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§6–8; Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2–6]

## 6. What Would Change The Valuation Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Make It Cheaper | What Would Make It More Expensive | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fairly valued — $237.01 base versus $254.69 price | A lower price while $12.06 NTM EPS and the 19.65x base-equivalent P/E remain intact, or realized cash flow begins to track above the DCF path without higher capital needs. | NTM EPS below $12.06, stalled margin gains, or capex staying near the current 6%–7% of sales range would weaken cash conversion and the warranted multiple. | **Single highest-value request:** one matched forward cash-flow dataset with consensus capex, working capital and FCFF through FY2030, including analyst counts, to test the $850.5m DCF path against the $1.641bn price-implied requirement. [Valuation 04 Intrinsic DCF, §§2–4; Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §2] |

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Use **$370.63 bull / $237.01 base / $66.31 cyclical-trough bear**, all on a 12-month horizon; the base is a 70% peer NTM P/E / 30% DCF blend. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§2–3]
- The $254.69 price implies 46.75% annual FCFF growth through FY2030 or a 13.85% EBIT margin under the DCF conventions; neither is proven, while holding the base cash path fixed implies a 6.95% discount rate. [Valuation 05 Reverse DCF, §§2–5]
- Margin of safety is **(7.46%)** to the $237.01 base; downside to the **$66.31** bear is **73.96%**. These are separate measures. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §4]
- This is not a controlling-owner value trap, but simple multiple reversion is risky: the old P/E series is not admissible, sector multiple history is unavailable, and business quality is 42/100 with a narrow, not yet economically proven moat. [Management-Governance 04 Ownership & Insider Behavior, §4; Valuation 02 Own History, §§4–6; Business Model 07 Business Quality, §1; Business Model 09 Moat, §5]
- Trust the matched peer NTM P/E most; keep DCF as the conservative cash-conversion check; give no weight to own-history reversion or SOTP. [Valuation 07 Scenario & Fair Value, §§1–2]
- The 126.94% method spread applies the hard valuation-confidence cap of 55; the final score is 50. No price, consensus, peer, terminal-dominance, owner, or cycle-distortion cap applies.
- The single highest-value next input is a matched consensus capex, working-capital and FCFF dataset through FY2030 with analyst counts.
- The master synthesizer's **Valuation and Peer Mispricing** section should defer to this synthesis; the fair-value **levels** here are the inputs for the master's probability-weighted scenario model, and the master assigns the probabilities.

## 8. Simple Summary

- The $254.69 price is 7.5% above the $237.01 base value, so BURL is fairly valued on the module's rule and has no cushion.
- The 12-month levels are **$370.63 bull, $237.01 base, and $66.31 cyclical-trough bear**.
- The market price implies **46.75% annual FCFF growth through FY2030** or a **13.85% EBIT margin**; neither is proven.
- The stated bear means **73.96% downside** to $66.31.
- The direct-peer NTM P/E matters most; DCF is the downside check. Own-history reversion and SOTP get no weight.
- No controlling-owner trap is present, but old-multiple reversion may be a trap because the historical basis is disputed and sector multiple history is missing.
- A fresh, pool-verified price was available; no price-related cap applies.

| Share count used for market cap | **62.8m** | [Capital IQ Comps→Financial Data, “Shares Outstanding Latest” (subject row), 2026-09-28; CIQ facts sidecar] |
| Share count used for per-share fair value | **63.896m** | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statement of Operations, p.6] |

The Q2 three-month diluted weighted average exceeds the Q2 basic weighted average of 62.867m by 1.029m shares (1.64%). Burlington says diluted EPS uses the treasury-stock method for options, restricted stock and RSUs, and the if-converted method for applicable convertible notes. The $254.69 September 28 close exceeds the 2027 notes’ stated initial $205.93 conversion price. Even so, the filing does not supply current option strikes, current unvested awards, or the exact net-share settlement effect needed to rebuild a September 28 treasury-stock-method and if-converted count. The 63.896m diluted weighted average is therefore the conservative per-share proxy, not a confirmed point-in-time fully diluted total. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statement of Operations, p.6; Note 4—Long-Term Debt, pp.12–13; Note 7—Earnings Per Share; Capital IQ Comps→Financial Data, “Day Close Price Latest,” 2026-09-28; CIQ facts sidecar]

The market-cap count is the latest pool-sourced shares-outstanding read, while per-share fair-value work uses the higher diluted proxy so it does not omit known dilution. The difference in dates is a stated limitation.

## 3. Market Capitalization

`Market cap = share count × current price`

`62.8m shares × $254.69 = $15,994.5m`, or **$16.0bn** (rounded).

The price and 62.8m share count are both from the same September 28 Capital IQ subject-company snapshot, as mechanically pinned in the CIQ facts sidecar. [Capital IQ Comps→Financial Data, “Day Close Price Latest” and “Shares Outstanding Latest” (subject row), 2026-09-28; CIQ facts sidecar]

The canonical EV is **$17.210bn**. It uses the filing-based gross financial debt from `balance-sheet-survival/01`, as required, and excludes operating leases from strict debt. This is a debt-definition choice, not a statement that lease commitments are immaterial: including the $3.993bn operating-lease liability produces a separate lease-inclusive obligation view of **$21.203bn** (`$17,210.3m + $3,992.6m`). [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 3, pp.10–11; balance-sheet-survival/01 Leverage Anchor Summary]

The required CIQ sidecar reports $5,906.1m total debt and $5,202.4m net debt at August 1, 2026. It reconciles to the lease-inclusive vendor basis: the $3,992.6m operating-lease liability plus financial debt carried after deferred financing costs. That vendor net-debt amount is **not** broad §15 net debt, because broad debt would mean financial debt less liquid short-term investments; it is a lease-inclusive obligation measure. The filing-based strict bridge above is canonical. [CIQ Financials→Balance Sheet, “Total Debt” and “Net Debt,” Q2 2026-08-01; CIQ facts sidecar; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5, 10, 12]

Cash quality: the $703.7m is cash and equivalents, with no separately reported liquid short-term investments and no separately reported restricted-cash balance. A $44.0m long-term-investment balance in the CIQ workbook is not identified as short-term or liquid, so it is not netted. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.5; Capital IQ Financials Annual workbook, Balance Sheet, Q2 FY2026 column—vendor export]

# Multiples — Own History — BURL

Burlington Stores, Inc. is a U.S. GAAP operating retailer and reports in USD. Fiscal periods are 52/53-week years ending near January 31. The $254.69 NYSE close (September 28, 2026), $17.210bn enterprise value (EV, the value of equity plus financial debt less cash), $1.216bn strict net debt and 63.896m diluted-share proxy below are inherited verbatim from `01_price-and-capital-structure`. The canonical EV excludes the separately disclosed $3.993bn operating-lease liability; this matters when comparing it with Capital IQ's vendor EV series. [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, pp.5, 10–13]

## 1. Current Multiples

| Multiple | Basis (LTM / NTM / FY) | Metric Value | Current Multiple | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| P / E | LTM diluted GAAP EPS | $11.13 / share | 22.88x | `$254.69 ÷ $11.13`; [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; data/BURL/Company Comparable Analysis Burlington Stores Inc.xls, Financial Data, subject row, 2026-09-28] |
| EV / EBITDA | LTM; Capital IQ standard EBITDA, not a GAAP subtotal | $1,360.7m | 12.65x | `$17,210.3m ÷ $1,360.7m`; [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Income Statement, LTM to 2026-08-01; ciq_facts.json, LTM EBITDA] |
| EV / EBIT | LTM; Capital IQ operating-income calculation | $951.6m | 18.09x | `$17,210.3m ÷ $951.6m`; [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; data/BURL/Company Comparable Analysis Burlington Stores Inc.xls, Financial Data, subject row, 2026-09-28] |
| EV / Sales | LTM reported net sales | $12,198.6m | 1.41x | `$17,210.3m ÷ $12,198.6m`; [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Income Statement, LTM to 2026-08-01] |
| P / Book | Latest book value per diluted-share proxy | $31.34 / share | 8.13x | `$254.69 ÷ $31.34`; [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, §6] |
| P / FCF / FCF yield | LTM normalised operating FCF | $357.0m | 44.80x / 2.23% | `$15,994.5m ÷ $357.0m`; normalised FCF = reported $412.5m less the $55.5m tariff-refund benefit. [earnings/06 Earnings Quality, §1; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, p.20] |
| Dividend yield | Trailing and forward | $0 declared | 0.0% | Burlington has not declared, and does not expect to declare in the near term, a common-stock dividend. [data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-K(Mar-19-2026).doc, Item 5—Dividends] |

The LTM FCF yield uses the conservative, normalised cash figure. Reported LTM FCF would instead give a 2.58% yield (`$412.5m ÷ $15,994.5m`), but the $55.5m refund is not a recurring operating input. [earnings/06 Earnings Quality, §§1 and 10; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, p.20]

**Capital IQ reconciliation.** The source-bound sidecar reports its latest historical `TEV/LTM EBITDA` close as **8.5x** at September 18, 2026 and its `P/LTM EPS` close as **21.3x**; those are the authoritative vendor reads and are not overwritten here. But the canonical strict-debt EV produces 12.65x on the same vendor LTM EBITDA. Separately, the CIQ comparable-company sheet gives a lease-inclusive TEV of $21.201bn and LTM EBITDA of $1.361bn, whose visible arithmetic is 15.58x, while its Trading Multiples sheet prints 9.0x. The 8.5x/9.0x figures therefore cannot be reconciled to either disclosed EV bridge from the frozen workbook. This is an unresolved vendor-definition or extraction-basis gap, not a reason to substitute a preferred number silently. [ciq_facts.json, `ev_ebitda_current_x`; data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet, latest Close; data/BURL/Company Comparable Analysis Burlington Stores Inc.xls, Financial Data and Trading Multiples, subject row, 2026-09-28]

## 2. Historical Multiple Bands (3–5 years)

The bands use the 16 quarterly `Close` observations from September 30, 2022 through June 30, 2026. The September 18, 2026 CIQ observation is shown separately as the vendor-current comparison and is excluded from the historical statistics. Percentile of range is `(current − historical minimum) ÷ (historical maximum − historical minimum)`, capped at 0%/100% if outside the range.

| Multiple | Min | Mean | Median | Max | Current | Percentile of Range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P / E | 28.51x | 40.95x | 39.40x | 81.01x | 22.88x anchor / 21.31x CIQ | Below range / 0% |
| EV / EBITDA | 8.27x | 10.83x | 11.12x | 13.23x | 12.65x canonical / 8.54x CIQ | 88% / 6% — not comparable |
| EV / EBIT | 25.18x | 31.56x | 30.80x | 47.16x | 18.09x canonical / 21.12x CIQ | Below range / 0% |
| EV / Sales | 1.27x | 1.72x | 1.76x | 1.98x | 1.41x canonical / 1.50x CIQ | 20% / 33% |

[data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet, `Close` rows for the 16 historical quarter-end columns and September 18, 2026 latest column; ciq_facts.json, `range_position`, `ev_ebitda_percentile`, `pe_ltm_current_x`]

The anchor-current figures use the strict-debt EV and September 28 price required by `01`; the CIQ-current figures use the vendor series' September 18 close. The 10-day price-date difference explains part of the P/E and EV/Sales gap, but it does not explain the EV/EBITDA identity failure described in §1. Historical `Multiples` is also labelled “Dilution: Basic,” whereas the anchor P/E uses diluted LTM EPS; this is a stated basis limitation on the P/E reversion read. [data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet, header; valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, §§1, 4 and 7]

## 3. Re-Rating / De-Rating Read

On the least-disputed equity-side measure, the anchor P/E of 22.88x is **44.1% below** its own 40.95x mean and **41.9% below** its 39.40x median: `(22.88 ÷ 40.95) − 1` and `(22.88 ÷ 39.40) − 1`. It is below the lowest one of the 16 historical closes, 28.51x. EV/Sales is also lower: 1.41x is **18.1% below** its 1.72x mean and **19.9% below** its 1.76x median. [data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet, `Close` rows; valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; earnings/01 Historical Financials, §2]

This is a de-rating versus BURL's own recorded P/E and EV/Sales history, not proof that the market is wrong. *Inference, not from filings:* the lower multiple is consistent with a mixed-quality, discretionary retail model: business quality is scored 42/100, current reported Q2 gross margin included a $55.5m tariff refund that management plans to reinvest, and the store/supply-chain build consumes substantial capital. The evidence does not establish that the old P/E premium remains warranted. [business-model/07 Business Quality, §§1–4; data/BURL/Burlington_Stores_Inc_-_Form_10-Q(Aug-27-2026).doc, p.20; data/BURL/BURL_Q2_2026_Earnings_PR.pdf, Outlook]

EV/EBIT also sits below its recorded range, but it is not independent confirmation. EV/EBITDA cannot be used in this read because its 8.54x vendor series close conflicts materially with both the canonical 12.65x calculation and the CIQ comparable-sheet arithmetic in §1. [data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet, `Close` rows; data/BURL/Company Comparable Analysis Burlington Stores Inc.xls, Financial Data and Trading Multiples, 2026-09-28]

## 4. Implied Value from Reversion

The required own-history base point is a **mechanical sensitivity, not an admissible fair-value input**: **$438.53 per share**, the 39.40x historical-median P/E applied to current $11.13 diluted LTM EPS. It is named because P/E has no EV bridge, but it still carries the basic-versus-diluted-history limitation. `07_scenario-and-fair-value` should not weight it as a clean base case unless it first resolves the vendor-basis conflicts and concludes that the historic P/E is warranted by current business quality. [data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet, `Close` P/E rows; valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; earnings/01 Historical Financials, §2]

| Multiple | Reversion Target (mean / median) | Implied EV or Equity | Implied Price/Share | vs Current Price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P / E | 40.95x / 39.40x | Equity $29.120bn / $28.020bn | $455.74 / **$438.53** | +78.9% / +72.2% |
| EV / Sales | 1.72x / 1.76x | EV $21.017bn / $21.473bn; equity $19.801bn / $20.257bn | $309.89 / $317.03 | +21.7% / +24.5% |

P/E arithmetic is `multiple × $11.13 EPS`; implied equity is then price × 63.896m diluted shares. EV/Sales arithmetic is `multiple × $12,198.6m LTM sales`; implied equity is EV less $1.216bn **strict** net debt, divided by 63.896m diluted shares. The median points across the two mechanically usable multiples span **$317.03–$438.53**, a $121.50 or 38.3%-of-low dispersion, rather than a corroborated range. [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary; earnings/01 Historical Financials, §2; data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet]

EV/EBITDA and EV/EBIT are deliberately excluded from the reversion table. Applying their vendor historical bands to strict-debt EV would silently mix the strict anchor with a vendor TEV basis; for EV/EBITDA, the reported current vendor multiple additionally fails the basic numerator/denominator identity. The reversion also assumes that the multiple was not structurally changed by quality, cyclicality, capital needs, or the current tariff-refund effect. Available business-model and earnings evidence does not prove that assumption. [valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, §§4–5; business-model/07 Business Quality, §4; earnings/06 Earnings Quality, §10]

## 5. Sector Cycle Reality Test

**Not assessable — no sector-level multiple history.** The frozen pool has BURL's own multiple series and a one-date peer snapshot, but no dated retail-sector P/E or EV/EBITDA series. As a limited price-only context, the SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT) rose from $56.59 on September 30, 2022 to $82.70 on September 28, 2026, or 46.1%; that return cannot distinguish earnings growth from a sector-multiple expansion and is therefore not evidence that BURL's own band is cycle-elevated or cycle-depressed. No `RF-VAL-001` or `RF-VAL-002` tag is warranted. [Web: FinanceCharts, XRT weekly close 2022-09-30 (indicative, unverified); Web: Stock Analysis, XRT close 2026-09-28 (indicative, unverified)]

## 6. Own-History Read

P/E and EV/Sales both place BURL below their recorded four-year ranges, but they produce materially different mechanical median values: $438.53 and $317.03 per share. The single biggest caveat is the unresolved Capital IQ enterprise-value basis: its historical EV/EBITDA close is 8.54x while the strict anchor yields 12.65x and its own comparable sheet does not reproduce either figure. Reversion to the historic P/E mean is not a clean base case until that data issue, the basic-versus-diluted P/E basis, the sector-cycle gap, and the case for a continuing historic multiple are resolved. [data/BURL/Burlington Stores Inc NYSE BURL Financials_Quarterly.xls, Multiples sheet; data/BURL/Company Comparable Analysis Burlington Stores Inc.xls, Financial Data and Trading Multiples, 2026-09-28; valuation/01 Price & Capital Structure, Anchor Summary]
